nodes.title: [Perf][DSV4.1] Overlap mHC coefficients for small TP batches
nodes.body:
## Purpose

Overlap shifted mHC coefficient generation with attention/FFN on small batches. The decoder keeps one post/pre path: the existing mHC dispatcher
selects overlap or native execution, while the decoder joins the coefficient
stream before consuming its outputs.

`supports_mhc_overlap` in `.ops.mhc` requires SM100/DeepGEMM, no ubatching,
and compatible projection dimensions: hidden width divisible by 64, and
`hc_mult * (hc_mult + 2)` a positive multiple of 8 no greater than 32.
The exact H5120/hc4 restrictions and helper assertion are removed.
Compatible tensor/data/pipeline/expert-parallel configurations, attention backends,
and LoRA configurations use the same token cutoff, without a separate performance
allowlist. Larger batches, draft layers, and piecewise/breakable graphs retain
native execution. The cutoff is generalized from the TP4 measurements below;
those measurements do not establish a gain for every newly enabled configuration.

The cutoff is **16 tokens**, based on same-instance paired full-forward
measurements with matching tuned GEMM tactics (three samples per arm):

| Tokens | Native ms | Overlap ms | Reduction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 4.763 | 4.692 | 1.49% |
| 6 | 6.204 | 5.929 | 4.42% |
| 8 | 6.644 | 6.360 | 4.28% |
| 12 | 7.408 | 7.292 | 1.57% |
| 16 | 7.966 | 7.877 | 1.12% |
| 24 | 9.153 | 9.365 | -2.31% |
| 48 | 11.915 | 12.040 | -1.05% |
| 96 | 15.292 | 15.247 | 0.29% |
| 192 | 18.820 | 18.977 | -0.84% |
| 252 | 20.040 | 20.230 | -0.95% |

All samples are retained; the 24/48-token overlap arms contain outliers
(SD 0.390/0.388 ms). Larger shapes show no reliable useful gain, so keep native
execution there. Selection uses the captured token shape, never actual KV
length. Split-kernel warmup is bounded by the same cutoff.

## Validation

Based on main `17e50b9b76`. Latest validation: **79 GPU tests pass**, covering
exact output parity and changed-input CUDA graph replay across `(hidden_size,
hc_mult)` = `(4096, 2)`, `(5120, 4)`, `(7168, 4)`, plus decoder/reference parity
and graph/batch fallbacks. Pre-commit passes.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/test_mhc_kernels.py \
  -k 'overlap_preserves_outputs or decoder_mixes_match_torch' -q -rs
```

Only transient input/scratch tensors (`x`, `mix`, `sqr`) need side-stream allocator
recording. The model retains weights, and callers retain coefficient outputs
until joining the side stream; the helper documents that ownership requirement.

Model/performance measurements below are prior results, not reruns on the new
main base or measurements of every newly enabled configuration.

Measured on GB200×4, model revision `dba1be0a40aa45a94ad051997016db3960a90277`,
FlashInfer 0.6.18.post1, TP4, DSpark fixed length 5, and synthetic 100K ±5% KV.
These are fixed-forward GPU latencies; no default-O2 piecewise-serving gain is
claimed. The prior ten-sample native/automatic pair measured 6.206→5.932 ms (4.42%).

The refactored commit's three-sample same-instance native/automatic comparison
measures **6.210→5.928 ms (4.55%)**, with identical inputs, KV and tuned GEMM
tactics. Automatic selection activates all 40 target layers. Both arms have
finite outputs and zero eager/graph, changed-input and restored-input replay
errors. Replay checks do not assert native/overlap full-model bitwise parity.

Prior matched real-weight GSM8K: 1271→1268/1319 (96.36→96.13%; 7 improve, 10 regress).
DSpark acceptance length 3.870→3.874. Local FP64 and serialized/async checks support
the numerical change; full-model hidden states are rounding-sensitive. The
refactor preserves the evaluated kernel math and launch order, so this accuracy
evaluation is reused. Prior same-instance allocator peaks increased 16 MiB allocated
and 74 MiB reserved per rank; this is not a serving-capacity measurement.

The projection-width limit of 32 follows DeepGEMM's device-side output-swizzle
constraint. Newly enabled dimensions have correctness coverage, not additional
end-to-end performance measurements.

## Final-head validation (2026-09-21)

Exact head `479b025e45`, GB200×4, pinned model revision above, TP4 **without
DSpark or all-reduce+mHC fusion**, FlashInfer FP8 attention/MXFP4 sparse indexer.
Baseline uses the same head with overlap disabled before loading.

| Metric | Overlap disabled | Enabled |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Forward-only, KV8704 | 4.727 /4.730 ms (before/after) | 4.657 ms (−1.5%) |
| Real8K/1K C1 mean TPOT | 5.013 ms | 4.992 ms (−0.4%) |
| Median ITL | 5.011 ms | 4.974 ms |
| P99 ITL | 5.228 ms | 6.049 ms |
| Full GSM8K flexible extraction | 1266/1319 (95.98%) | 1271/1319 (96.36%) |

Forward harness: same initialized synthetic weights/KV, five samples ×20
CUDA-graph replays after5s warmup per arm; slowest-rank GPU time, excluding
lm_head/sampling/scheduler/HTTP. All arms pass finite-output and changed-input
replay checks (zero replay error). This is not cross-arm bitwise parity.

Serving: ten exact8192-input/1024-output requests per arm, greedy, C1, two
warmups; FULL_DECODE_ONLY with eager prefill. All requests succeed; candidate
tail bursts in2/10 requests mean this is not a strong serving-speed claim.
GSM8K: lm-eval0.4.12, five-shot chat, greedy, seed123, C8, max output1024;
matching prompts/targets,10 improve and5 regress, strict formatting79.68% both.

**Warmup caveat:** initial overlap-disabled GSM8K reproduced cached FlashInfer
CuTe tactic compilation under strict JIT monitoring. Final arms use identical
startup-only cached-tactic and DeepGEMM split warmup from the existing fix in
#57643, plus identical pinned tactics. Zero monitored runtime JIT afterward;
these workarounds are not part of this PR. No claim of stock-stack zero JIT or
coverage of every newly enabled topology/backend. The79 focused GPU tests
above validate the exact head.

## Duplicate-work check

No open PR found for shifted mHC coefficient/sublayer overlap. #52725 concerns
XPU norm fusion; #42735 changes BF16 shared staging in the older mHC kernel;
#56761 changes GLM JIT warmup; #51802 registers NVIDIA V4 warmup variants.
None implements this scheduling change.

AI assistance was used to implement, benchmark and test this change.

nodes.title: [Bugfix][KV Connector] Propagate cache reset failure during sleep
nodes.body:
## Purpose

Check the cache-reset result during sleep/pause instead of continuing to sleep after a failed reset.

Only `vllm/v1/engine/core.py` changes:
- Check the prefix-cache reset result immediately and raise on failure, before clearing MM/encoder caches or sleeping.
- Complete deferred pause Futures with the exception when pause finalization fails, or with success when it finishes normally.

Related work: #53082 restructures sleep/pause. This fix is limited to consuming the cache-reset result and propagating deferred failures through the Future; it does not duplicate that refactor.

## Validation

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest -o addopts= -q tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py::test_scheduler_reset_prefix_cache tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py::test_reset_connector_cache_no_connector_is_no_op_success tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_mooncake_store_connector.py::test_scheduler_reset_connector_cache_invokes_connector_reset
```

Result: 3 passed.

After the idle-callback change, an inline CPU probe of the production EngineCore methods with a mocked connector/executor passed all 5 checks: synchronous and deferred sleep with successful and failed resets, plus preservation of the original pause-finalization exception in the Future. Failed resets never invoke executor sleep; idle callbacks do not leak the finalization error.

Pre-commit checks and mypy 3.12 passed. Validation covers mocked lifecycle and scheduler/connector behavior, not a live remote KV service or model evaluation. No test files are added.

AI assistance (Codex) was used for simplification and validation.

nodes.title: [ROCm][DSv4.1] Keep the Engram tables in host memory on ROCm
nodes.body:
## Purpose

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash's Engram n-gram tables are the largest single consumer of device memory — 47.2 GiB per rank at TP=4, about a third of everything the weights hold. CUDA moves them to pinned host memory and reads them over UVA (#56512); on ROCm two `is_cuda()` gates turn that off, so `engram_config` stays `None`, `amd/model.py` falls through to the base `Engram`, and the tables stay on the accelerator.

Nothing in the offload path is platform-specific — `get_accelerator_view_from_cpu_tensor()` already dispatches on `is_cuda_alike()`, and `hipHostRegister` backs pinned host memory — so widen the two gates and import `Engram` from `..nvidia.engram`, as `amd/model.py` already does for `DeepseekV41ModelState`. No new AMD code. The `cpu_offload` tests in `tests/kernels/test_engram.py` carried the same gate and are widened too. `DPSharedEngramStorage` and the DP head sharding arrive with the import but stay inert at `data_parallel_size=1`.

Duplicate-work check (2026-09-18): #56512 (merged) built the NVIDIA offload and left these gates behind; #56926, #57195 and #56757 continue that path and none touches `amd/` or the gates — #56757's `disk_offload_dir` requires `cpu_offload=True`, so it is blocked on ROCm by the same gate. #56400 has an AMD/ROCm section with no engram item. Prior art: SemiAnalysisAI/InferenceX#3217 by @functionstackx reached the same design as a local patch for an MI355X TP2 recipe, and recorded that hardware evidence was the outstanding gate before upstreaming. `vllm/config/engram.py` is also edited by those three, so this needs a rebase onto whichever merges first.

## Test plan

```bash
python -m pytest tests/kernels/test_engram.py -q
python -m ruff check vllm/config/engram.py vllm/config/vllm.py \
  vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/model.py tests/kernels/test_engram.py
python -m ruff format --check vllm/config/engram.py vllm/config/vllm.py \
  vllm/models/deepseek_v41/amd/model.py tests/kernels/test_engram.py
git diff --check

# MI355X (gfx950), ROCm 7.2.3, TP=4, one session per arm, warmup then 3 reps
vllm serve $MODEL --tensor-parallel-size 4 --language-model-only \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --trust-remote-code --moe-backend aiter \
  --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 --max-model-len 33792 --max-num-seqs 128 \
  --max-cudagraph-capture-size 1024 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384
vllm bench serve --backend vllm --endpoint /v1/completions --model $MODEL \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len 4096 --random-output-len 512 \
  --random-range-ratio 0 --num-prompts 32 --max-concurrency 8 --seed 1234 \
  --ignore-eos
python tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py --port 8000 --num-questions 1319 \
  --num-shots 5 --max-concurrency 64

# DP shared storage, TP=2 / DP=2
vllm serve $MODEL --tensor-parallel-size 2 --data-parallel-size 2 \
  --engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true,"dp_shared_memory":true}' ...
```

## Test result

- `tests/kernels/test_engram.py` on gfx950: the two `cpu_offload` tests are the reason for the test change in this PR. Their gates were `is_cuda()`, so on ROCm the whole file was 9 passed / 75 skipped and the offload path had no coverage at all. Widened to `is_cuda_alike()`, `test_engram_lookup_matches_torch` (2 cpu_offload x 2 background x 3 token counts) and `test_engram_head_shards_reconstruct_checkpoint` (2 cpu_offload x 4 TP sizes) give **20 passed**, including the bit-exact comparison against the torch dequant reference reading from pinned host memory.
- The alias is coherent on gfx950, which is what the stricter `is_uva_available()` proposed in #57404 probes for: host writes made after the accelerator view is taken are visible to the device, and device writes are visible to the host, for uint8 and float8_e4m3fn at 4 KiB and 1 MiB.
- ruff check, ruff format --check and `git diff --check` pass on all four files. mypy and pre-commit were not run — neither is installed on the test host.
- TP=4 serving: the offload log line appears once per rank per layer (8 lines, 23.60 GiB each), and `Resolved Engram configuration` appears at all, which it does not on base.
- TP=2 / DP=2 with `dp_shared_memory`: server comes up and serves, four shared allocations of 47.21 GiB logged as "shared across DP replicas", 190 GiB resident in `/dev/shm`, no errors. That run is also the only one that reaches `verify_model_config()`, the second gate, since only an explicitly supplied `--engram-config` gets there. Functional check only; no DP performance claim is made.

## Model evaluation

`tests/evals/gsm8k/gsm8k_eval.py`, all 1319 problems, five-shot, concurrency 64, MI355X TP=4:

| | accuracy | invalid rate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| base | 0.8999 | 0.15% |
| this PR | 0.9030 | 0.08% |

+0.31 pp against a 1.16 pp standard error for the difference of two proportions, z = 0.27. The acceptance band was fixed before the run. A second offload build measured 0.9052 (z = 0.46); see the note under Performance.

## Performance

The prefetch is what keeps this free. In the shape Engram actually issues — 3 n-gram orders x 6 local hash heads = 18 rows of 256 B per token, in 2 of 40 layers — a UVA gather matches HBM at decode batch sizes and falls behind only at prefill batch sizes:

| tokens/step | rows | UVA view | HBM | delta |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 18 | 9.3 us | 10.7 us | -1.4 us |
| 32 | 576 | 9.9 us | 9.8 us | +0.1 us |
| 256 | 4608 | 25.6 us | 9.9 us | +15.7 us |
| 1024 | 18432 | 89.0 us | 10.3 us | +78.7 us |

The model-owned prefetch stream, with `background=True` leaving half the SMs to the main stream, covers the last two rows.

**KV cache capacity**, TP=4, identical across three independent starts:

| | base | this PR | delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Available KV cache memory | 107.8 GiB | 154.38 GiB | **+43.2%** |
| GPU KV cache size | 4,325,113 tokens | 6,194,599 tokens | **+43.2%** |
| Max concurrency @ 33,792 ctx | 127.99x | 183.32x | **+43.2%** |

Predicted from the startup memory breakdown beforehand as +43.8%; the measurement met it within 0.4%.

At TP=2 / DP=2 each rank carries a wider engram shard (47.21 GiB per layer instead of 23.60), so the same change is correspondingly larger. Both arms are the same topology and flags; the base arm simply cannot be given `--engram-config`, because that is the gate this PR widens:

| | base | this PR | delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Available KV cache memory | 57.65 GiB | 151.45 GiB | **+162.7%** |
| GPU KV cache size | 2,313,707 tokens | 6,078,307 tokens | **+162.7%** |

The startup breakdown pins down what moved: per rank, "consumed memory (weights + non-torch)" is 182.05 GiB on base and 87.62 GiB with the offload, a difference of 94.43 GiB against the 94.42 GiB the two engram shards occupy at this TP.

**Serving throughput**, TP=4, random 4096 in / 512 out, 32 prompts, concurrency 8, three repetitions each (mean +/- sd). "paired" is the offload arm measured back to back with base in one session; "shipped" is this PR's exact diff, measured separately:

| | base | offload, paired | offload, shipped |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| mean TPOT | 11.35 +/- 0.02 ms | 11.35 +/- 0.02 ms | 11.35 +/- 0.00 ms |
| median TPOT | 11.22 +/- 0.01 ms | 11.24 +/- 0.02 ms | 11.24 +/- 0.00 ms |
| p99 TPOT | 12.54 +/- 0.01 ms | 12.54 +/- 0.02 ms | 12.56 +/- 0.01 ms |
| mean TTFT | 796.88 +/- 2.43 ms | 794.08 +/- 0.35 ms | 799.97 +/- 1.61 ms |
| p99 TTFT | 1061.31 +/- 1.69 ms | 1054.38 +/- 2.59 ms | 1063.68 +/- 4.60 ms |
| output throughput | 620.64 +/- 0.97 tok/s | 621.10 +/- 1.06 tok/s | 620.61 +/- 0.11 tok/s |

Paired against base: +0.46 tok/s on a pooled standard error of 0.83, t = 0.55. Shipped against the same base: -0.03 tok/s, -0.005%. Flat either way, p99 included. There are two offload columns because the paired arm reached the offload path through the local copy of `nvidia/engram.py` described above, which is not the diff here; the shipped diff reproduces it exactly, down to the same KV cache figures and offload log lines.

Host cost at TP=4: 47.2 GiB x 4 ranks = 188.8 GiB of pinned host memory, against 2954 GiB of RAM on the test node. Containers need `--ulimit memlock=-1`.

AI assistance was used for this change. Every changed line was reviewed by the submitter, and the measurements above were produced by the submitter on the hardware named.

nodes.title: [Profiler] Unify platform-aware torch profiling
nodes.body:
## Purpose

Implement the A+B+C profiler-core split proposed in #56542:

- rebuild the one-shot `torch.profiler.profile` object for every profiling round (addresses #45987)
- add configurable, platform-validated worker activities while preserving CPU, CUDA, and XPU defaults
- skip worker annotation computation when a CUDA-only torch profile cannot record it
- centralize ordinary profiler logic across GPU, CPU, and XPU workers without changing the profiling RPC/API signatures
  - CPU profiler now also honors `profile_prefix`

## Duplicate-work assessment

Consolidates two currently conflicted PRs after the split recommendation on #56542:

- #45992 only rebuilds the inner one-shot torch profiler. This PR incorporates that approach and additionally handles platform activities and the shared worker lifecycle.
- #55751 adds the activity field, but does not validate activities against the concrete worker platform, preserve frontend CPU semantics for CUDA-only profiling, avoid annotation computation, or centralize CPU/GPU/XPU construction.

Both PRs have been cross-linked, and their authors/work are credited here.

## Test plan and results

pytest tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_profiler.py -q 
# 122 passed

pytest \
  tests/v1/engine/test_async_llm.py::test_cuda_profiler_requests_reach_engine_core \

nodes.title: [Build] Fix DeepGEMM CUDA 12.9 release builds
nodes.body:
## Purpose

Restore the six CUDA 12.9 release targets that fail in [release-v2 #6858](https://buildkite.com/vllm/release-v2/builds/6858): x86_64 and aarch64 wheels, plus both architectures' default and Ubuntu 24.04 images.

All six fail while compiling DeepGEMM's host extension because `layout/mega_mhc.cuh` uses `__nv_fp8_e4m3` without including `<cuda_fp8.h>`. CUDA 13's transitive includes mask the missing declaration; CUDA 12.9 does not. The subsequent `y_fp8` errors are consequences of that missing type.

Update both synchronized DeepGEMM pins from `a6bbb800` to the merged upstream commit [e1f418c2](https://github.com/vllm-project/DeepGEMM/commit/e1f418c2a4f20818221f6b0e578b4c2f634d4c3f) from [DeepGEMM#12](https://github.com/vllm-project/DeepGEMM/pull/12). The dependency delta is exactly five include lines in two headers; it preserves all current SM90/SM120 and Mega MoE changes.

## Duplicate-work check

The header fix is merged in DeepGEMM#12; this PR consumes that work in vLLM and does not propose another upstream implementation. The merged commit has vLLM's current pin as its sole parent. The original duplicate-work checks found no competing open vLLM integration PR or matching open issue for `mega_mhc.cuh`.

## Validation

The merged pin `e1f418c2` and previously tested cherry-pick `70874eca` have the identical Git tree `cd1947d66f49ef498fdeb6f227bb9e52b5ba0787` (including submodule gitlinks). `git diff --exit-code 70874eca e1f418c2` passes with no changes. Local pre-commit, shell syntax, and diff checks were rerun after updating the pin. The six native builds below tested this identical dependency content under the earlier SHA; they were not rerun for this metadata-only pin replacement.

- `git diff --check`: passed in both vLLM and DeepGEMM.
- `bash -n tools/install_deepgemm.sh`: passed.
- `pre-commit run --files cmake/external_projects/deepgemm.cmake tools/install_deepgemm.sh`: all applicable hooks passed, including shellcheck and configuration validation.
- Confirmed the new dependency commit has the old pin as its sole parent and changes only the five include lines from DeepGEMM#12.
- Focused `g++ -std=c++20 -fsyntax-only` test including both layout headers: CUDA 12.9 reproduced the exact `__nv_fp8_e4m3` baseline failure and passed after the patch; CUDA 13.0 passed before and after. CUDA 12.9 headers came from NVIDIA runtime 12.9.79, nvcc 12.9.86, and CCCL 12.9.27 packages. Tested with the pinned CUTLASS headers in an x86_64 Linux container.
- Verified `git patch-id --stable` matches the original DeepGEMM#12 patch exactly.
- Native build validation: [release-v2 #6874](https://buildkite.com/vllm/release-v2/builds/6874), **passed: all six affected targets**. The validation branch uses the original PR head `55b0863c` plus a temporary build-only pipeline for the six affected targets. It retains release build arguments, verifies the five CPython DeepGEMM binaries in each wheel/image, and imports torch/vLLM in final images. It contains no wheel, image, or nightly publication steps.

| Target | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Build wheel - aarch64 - CUDA 12.9 | [Passed](https://buildkite.com/vllm/release-v2/builds/6874#01a0b43e-a7b0-441f-a694-d3d663dd1bf8) |
| Build wheel - x86_64 - CUDA 12.9 | [Passed](https://buildkite.com/vllm/release-v2/builds/6874#01a0b43e-a7b6-4b40-97a6-5fdb6254efb6) |

nodes.title: [Perf][DSV4.1] Fuse TP all-reduce with mHC input preparation
nodes.body:
## Purpose

Fuse TP all-reduce, mHC post mixing, delayed collapse, and RMSNorm at DSV4.1 decoder boundaries. This replaces three launches with one, preserves the BF16 boundaries, and retains coefficient overlap. The kernel reuses the existing MNNVL workspace without an additional persistent communication allocation.

Enabled by default for eligible SM100 TP4 forwards with 1–16 tokens, including speculative decoding. The selector requires hidden size 5120, hc_mult=4, EP disabled, and a multicast workspace; it does not restrict DP/PP size, LoRA, or attention backend. The existing overlap-support checks still apply, including disabling overlap for ubatching. Larger batches and graph boundaries use the existing operations. Sixteen is the largest size with a validated gain, not a measured crossover.

Builds on #57603, now merged into main, which overlaps coefficient computation but does not fuse collectives. This differs from #51244's terminal mHC/head fusion. Open-PR searches for `mhc allreduce` and `mhc fusion` found no duplicate of this decoder-boundary collective fusion.

The independent startup warmup fixes have been extracted: DeepGEMM mHC projection coverage is in #57843, and cached FlashInfer MXFP8 tactics are in #57842. Neither is included in this fusion PR.

## Communication choice and token cutoff

Keep multicast and the 16-token cutoff. A controlled GB200 TP4 experiment replaced multicast stores with explicit stores to each of the four peers, retaining the same math, Lamport synchronization, cleanup, and PDL. Push did not consistently improve performance:

| Tokens | Multicast kernel | Push kernel | Multicast model forward | Push model forward |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | 14.348 µs | 14.634 µs | 4.054 ms | 4.060 ms |
| 8 | 14.395 µs | 14.972 µs | 5.724 ms | 5.728 ms |
| 16 | 13.910 µs | 15.795 µs | 7.133 ms | 7.130 ms |

Kernel timings use cold-L2 CUDA-graph replay, five samples of 50 replays, and the maximum rank time. Model timings use the same synthetic-weight model instance, KV8704, identical tactics, and three samples of 20 replays; they exclude the output head and serving. Multicast and push model outputs were byte-identical on every rank at all nine tested sizes (1–128).

Extending fusion to 24, 32, 48, 64, 96, and 128 tokens regressed model-forward time in this screen, despite isolated kernel gains; coefficient overlap remained disabled above 16. Some nonstandard sizes used default tactics because exact cache buckets were absent. A follow-up using normal serving autotune buckets confirmed the gain at 1 and 16 tokens (4.667→4.060 ms and 7.783→7.127 ms). Near-boundary runs at 17 and 20 tokens failed the unfused baseline's native-top-k correctness check, so no timings from those shapes are accepted. This supports retaining 16 conservatively; it does not establish the exact crossover. No new model accuracy evaluation was run for the experimental variants.

Multicast requires a supported NVLink/NVSwitch configuration and successful group memory setup; GPU generation alone does not establish support. Explicit peer stores could broaden support to Hopper-or-newer systems with suitable peer-memory access without multicast. That would require separate allocation/dispatch support and hardware validation: this PR remains SM100 TP4, and the experimental push variant reused the existing workspace. Push is a possible portability fallback, not a demonstrated GB200 performance improvement.

## Latest model-forward comparison against main

Measured candidate `dd63c1fa00` (runtime source identical to the subsequently merged PR head `7be123b000`) versus main `d2983f2f16` fetched at benchmark start, including merged overlap and the latest DSpark block-table fix in both arms. GB200 ×4, TP4/DP1, FlashInfer FP8 attention, MXFP4 sparse-logits indexer, auto MoE, KV8704, max model length 1M. Matched synthetic weights/KV and 210 cached tactics with normal hybrid token buckets. Five samples ×20 full-forward CUDA-graph replays after warmup, maximum rank time per sample; median reported below.

| Mode | Batch | Component / tokens | Main | Candidate | Reduction |
| --- | ---: | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| No DSpark | 1 | main / 1 | 4.651 ms | 4.055 ms | 12.8% |
| No DSpark | 8 | main / 8 | 6.236 ms | 5.668 ms | 9.1% |
| No DSpark | 16 | main / 16 | 7.806 ms | 7.127 ms | 8.7% |
| DSpark | 1 | main / 6 | 5.867 ms | 5.280 ms | 10.0% |
| DSpark | 1 | draft / 5 | 0.353 ms | 0.344 ms | 2.4% |

DSpark uses fixed draft length5. These are model-forward measurements, excluding the output head, sampling, scheduling, HTTP and acceptance effects. The draft implementation is unchanged, so its small difference is not attributed directly to fusion. All accepted cases pass eager/graph and changed/restored-input replay checks with zero error. Initialization manifests and source/final tactic hashes match between arms.

An additional candidate DSpark B2 target case failed the harness native-top-k score check at layer2; no timing from that shape is accepted, and main B2 was not measured. This run does not establish B2 correctness or new model accuracy. Untimed setup permits compilation and strict JIT checking resumes before validation/timing; neither arm includes the extracted startup fixes #57842/#57843. The comparison measures warmed execution.

## Test Result

GB200 ×4, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash revision `dba1be0a40aa45a94ad051997016db3960a90277`, TP4/DP1, FlashInfer FP8 attention, MXFP4 sparse-logits indexer, auto MoE, no DSpark. Baseline disables only this fusion before model construction; it includes #57603. Both arms use the same checkpoint, configuration and FlashInfer autotuning cache (all 168 entries reused, checksum unchanged).

The latest polling/RMSNorm follow-up loads peer payloads together and distributes norm partials for local shared-memory reads. PDL completion stays early for multi-token forwards and moves to the end for one token. Compared with the previous fused kernel, a same-instance synthetic KV8704 forward comparison measured B1 4.558/4.588→4.044/4.044 ms, B8 6.014/6.012→5.969/5.979 ms, and B16 7.787/7.782→7.794/7.822 ms. B1 baseline varied between runs (4.184 ms in the prior controlled run), so the largest paired percentage is not a robust gain estimate. B16 is 0.1–0.5% slower in the final screen. Output bytes match on every rank for all three sizes; the final collective test also covers signed-zero sentinel collisions.

The serving and GSM8K measurements below are from the initial fused implementation (`fa59bb3883`). They have not been rerun after this output-equivalent follow-up.

8K input / 1K output serving, concurrency 1, three requests per run, forced output length:

| Run | Mean TPOT | Median ITL | P99 ITL |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Baseline | 4.947 ms | 4.951 ms | 5.034 ms |
| Candidate, initial | 5.361 ms | 4.510 ms | 16.240 ms |
| Candidate, repeat after GSM8K | 4.578 ms | 4.506 ms | 7.676 ms |

The warmed repeat reduces mean TPOT by 7.5%, but the initial candidate had stalls and tail latency remains higher. These short serving runs do not establish a tail-latency improvement. All requests completed, with 8192 input and 1024 output tokens each.

A separate fixed-forward screen measured B8 6.565→6.028 ms (−8.2%) and B16 8.421→7.785 ms (−7.6%). B32 exercises fallback: 11.382→11.353 ms with identical output. These are three-sample synthetic-weight/cache measurements at KV8704, excluding the output head and serving.

Full GSM8K, 1319 questions, five-shot chat, thinking disabled, greedy generation, seed 123, maximum 1024 generated tokens, concurrency 8:

| Metric | Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Flexible extraction | 1267/1319 (96.06%) | 1275/1319 (96.66%) |
| Strict match | 79.08% | 79.98% |

Prompt and target hashes match for every question. Floating-point ordering changes outputs; this is not bitwise model equivalence. The paired results have 11 candidate-only correct answers and 3 baseline-only correct answers.

- Four-GPU collective test passed: changing sizes, all-gather interleaving in the shared workspace, changed-input CUDA-graph replay.
- mHC regression selection: 137 passed.
- 77 saved real operator inputs: maximum relative RMS 2.3e-5 for residuals and 1.5e-4 for normalized inputs.
- CMake `_C_stable_libtorch` build and pre-commit checks passed.



Serving uses max model length 1048576, max sequences 8, max batched tokens 8192, 10 GiB KV cache, prefix caching disabled, Engram CPU offload, and `--compilation-config '{"mode":0,"cudagraph_mode":"FULL_DECODE_ONLY","cudagraph_capture_sizes":[1,2,4,8]}'`. The sequence cap is a validation setting, not a recipe recommendation.

AI assistance was used for implementation and validation. The human submitter confirmed review and relevant tests for the original submission; the warmup follow-up validation is reported separately below.

## Warmup validation

The sparse-candidate alignment fix and its tests were extracted into #57667. The validation below was run on combined commit `2219a281f8`, before the split, and includes that fix.

The missing mHC specialization was DeepGEMM split=4, not a TileLang epilogue. Warmup now covers splits 1/4/16 for both projection widths on GB200. A fresh-cache test compiled six variants, then successfully checked 26 runtime shapes with further compiler invocations forbidden.

A fresh real-weight TP4 server with `enable_jit_warmup=true` and `--jit-monitor-mode error --jit-monitor-verbose` completed 23 requests (736 generated tokens), spanning 3–8192 prompt tokens and mixed batches of up to eight requests. All four ranks enabled the monitor before requests: zero runtime Triton/TileLang/CuTeDSL JIT events, and no DeepGEMM compiler commands in this run. The 66 focused tests below and pre-commit checks passed.

The original serving measurements above explicitly disabled JIT warmup. These fixes close reproduced intermediate-prefill compilation gaps; they do not establish the cause of the original decode tails or a new steady-state speedup. GSM8K was not repeated for this startup/specialization follow-up, which leaves model arithmetic unchanged.

## Test Plan

```bash
RAY_ADDRESS=local .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/distributed/test_custom_all_reduce.py -k all_reduce_mhc -q -rs
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/kernels/test_mhc_kernels.py \
  -k 'deepseek_v41 or delayed_custom_op' -q -rs
```

```bash

  tests/model_executor/test_flashinfer_autotune_warmup.py \
  tests/model_executor/layers/test_mla_short_prefill_indexer.py \
  -k 'not sparse_mqa_logits_prefill_matches_dense_masked and not deep_select' -q -rs
```

## Rebase validation

Rebased onto main `9b49f92344` (merged #57603). Retained the simplified overlap helper and existing fusion eligibility, multicast transport, and 16-token cutoff. The fused CUDA kernel and dispatcher are unchanged. Dropped the obsolete extraction commit so the sparse-indexer alignment fix already on main remains intact.

At `75e3082ab1`, all pre-commit hooks passed and the focused GB200 GPU suite passed (176 passed, 135 deselected):

```bash
RAY_ADDRESS=local .venv/bin/python -m pytest \

  -k 'all_reduce_mhc or deepseek_v41 or delayed_custom_op' -q -rs
```

Serving benchmarks and GSM8K were not repeated for this rebase; the earlier results above retain their stated scope.

## Broader dispatch validation

Removed benchmark-only restrictions on DP/PP size, attention backend, LoRA, and speculative decoding. The TP4 group, fixed kernel dimensions, EP exclusion, and multicast workspace checks remain. The kernel and 16-token cutoff are unchanged. The distributed replay test now includes 6/12-token fixed verification and shrinking/growing token counts.

The completed TP4 DSpark comparison (2026-09-19, before the rebase) used draft length five, FlashInfer FP8 attention, the same checkpoint and matched 210-entry tactics. Baseline retained overlap and disabled only fusion. Both arms scored 125/128 on a matched GSM8K subset; mean acceptance lengths were 3.739 and 3.730. All ten 8K-input/1K-output serving requests per arm succeeded. Mean TPOT was 1.451→1.247 ms, but random-prompt acceptance also changed (5.241→5.803), so this is not an isolated fusion speedup.

That validation used identical pinned-tactic and startup warmup workarounds in both arms. It is a subset accuracy check for fixed DSpark, not validation of every admitted backend, topology, LoRA configuration, or speculative method. Adaptive shape changes are covered at the distributed-kernel level. No new full GSM8K evaluation was run for this dispatch-only follow-up.

nodes.title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Stop dummy draft decode steps from writing KV through stale block-table rows
nodes.body:
## Purpose

Fix a KV-cache corruption in Model Runner V2 speculative decoding under data parallelism: an idle DP rank's dummy batch runs the drafter's multi-step decode, which computes real slot mappings through the *persistent* per-slot block tables using `idx_mapping = arange(num_reqs)` (real request-state slots whose rows are stale), and writes drafter-layer K/V into offsets `1..k-1` of the first block of whatever request last occupied those slots. Those blocks are typically already registered in the prefix cache, so every later request that hits them reads corrupted drafter K/V while the target model's K/V stays intact.

Observed on GLM-5.2 (glm_moe_dsa, MTP k=5, DP=4 EP, prefix caching) as a per-request, exactly-zero MTP acceptance (`p0 = 0.0000`, `acc_len = 1.0`, `drafts == max_tokens`) that latches onto a conversation and disappears after `POST /reset_prefix_cache`; the poisoned rows were NaN (fp8 `0x7F`) in `model.layers.78.self_attn.attn`, with the target layers and indexer cache of the same block clean. On current main the same stale write still happens on every idle step (the written values happen to be finite there, so acceptance is unaffected), i.e. the write path is latent.

#49757 protected the read side (`get_dummy_block_tables` zeroes `input_block_tables`) and the target's dummy slot mappings are PAD (`prepare_dummy_attn`), but `_compute_slot_mappings_kernel` reads `block_table_ptrs` (the persistent tables), which neither protection covers.

## Fix

- `_compute_slot_mappings_kernel`: a row with `idx_mapping < 0` (dummy or CUDA-graph padding request) emits `PAD_SLOT_ID` and never dereferences a negative block-table row.
- `AutoRegressiveSpeculator.propose(dummy_run=True)`: mark every dummy row with `idx_mapping = -1` (already the speculator's convention for padded rows, ignored by `gumbel_sample`).

The guard lives in the kernel rather than in Python because the fused multi-step path re-runs `compute_slot_mappings` inside the captured CUDA graph between draft steps; only the kernel can neutralize a replayed dummy run.

## Test Plan

- `tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_block_table.py::test_dummy_request_slot_mapping_is_pad` (new): `idx_mapping == -1` yields all-PAD slot mappings; a real row still resolves through its block table.
- End-to-end on 4x GB200 with GLM-5.2 NVFP4, DP=4 + EP, `--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":5}'`, prefix caching on, fp8 KV, block 64, `FULL_DECODE_ONLY` graphs (the production decode geometry), driven by a growing-prefix multi-turn probe plus a unique-prompt load/probe "transition hunt":
  - f94666b60d unpatched: hunt trial 1 flips DEAD; 4/4 dead requests hit the same poisoned first block, all healthy requests on that rank do not; dumped drafter K/V rows 1-4 of that block are NaN.
  - f94666b60d + this fix: semantic gate passed, 3x20 chain requests 0 dead, 6/6 hunt trials 0 dead (mean p0 0.61-0.76); 66,164 dummy draft decode steps logged, every slot mapping PAD.
  - main dc07f1638f + this fix: semantic gate passed, 3x20 chain requests 0 dead, 6 hunt trials 0 dead; the dummy draft steps log `slots=[-1]`.

## Test Result

```
$ pytest -q tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_block_table.py      # GB200, main + fix
10 passed
$ pre-commit run --files vllm/v1/worker/gpu/block_table.py vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/autoregressive/speculator.py vllm/v1/worker/gpu/spec_decode/multi_module_mtp/speculator.py tests/v1/worker/test_gpu_block_table.py
all hooks passed
```

End-to-end reproducer (4x GB200, GLM-5.2 NVFP4, DP=4 EP, MTP k=5, prefix caching, fp8 KV, block 64, FULL_DECODE_ONLY):

| tree | chain probe (3x20) | transition hunt | dummy draft slots |
|---|---|---|---|
| f94666b60d (production) | 0 dead | trial 1 DEAD (1/6, then 1/6 and 2/6 on confirm) | real slots; poisoned block rows 1-4 NaN |
| f94666b60d + fix | 0 dead | 6/6 trials 0 dead | 66,164 steps, all PAD |
| main dc07f1638f | 0 dead | 6/6 trials 0 dead | real slots (finite values) |
| main dc07f1638f + fix | 0 dead | 6/6 trials 0 dead | all PAD |

The acceptance metrics above (mean p0 0.61-0.79 in every healthy run) double as the model-quality check: the change only affects dummy batches, and the semantic gate (answer planted at the prompt tail) passed in every run.

## Notes

- Duplicate check: `gh issue list`/`gh pr list` searches for the dummy-run / stale block table / draft KV path found no existing report; the closest related changes are #49757 (read-side zeroing) and #55458 (excludes DP padding rows from draft attention metadata; likely why the written values are finite on main).
- A follow-up could make read and write sides share one source by computing slot mappings from the per-batch gathered `input_block_tables`; this PR is the minimal, backportable fix.
- AI assistance: this change was investigated and drafted with Claude Code and reviewed with Codex; the submitter has reviewed every line and run the tests above.

nodes.title: [Bugfix] Fix Whisper engine crash on audio clips longer than 30s
nodes.body:
## Purpose

Offline `LLM.generate` with Whisper and an audio clip longer than 30 s kills the engine on main and on v0.29.0:

```
RuntimeError: The size of tensor a (1750) must match the size of tensor b (1500) at non-singleton dimension 0
```

Every later request then fails with `EngineDeadError`. v0.26.0 accepts the same input and truncates the clip to 30 s, which is what the HF feature extractor does by default.

The cause is the same as in #56912 (Qwen2-Audio). Since #53275 the multimodal processor passes `truncation=False` to the HF processor so that the placeholder text is not cut. `WhisperProcessor` forwards the same kwarg to `WhisperFeatureExtractor`, which then stops truncating audio to its 30 s window. A 35 s clip becomes 3500 frames, which is 1750 positions after the conv, and the encoder has 1500.

The fix is the same line as in #56912: `WhisperMultiModalProcessor._get_hf_mm_inputs` passes `truncation=True`. Clips of up to 30 s are processed exactly as before.

`/v1/audio/transcriptions` and `/v1/audio/translations` are not affected, because the server splits audio into chunks of at most 30 s before it reaches the processor, and Whisper does not serve the other endpoints. Only offline use with a longer clip hits this.

I did not find an existing issue or PR for this (searched for whisper truncation, whisper 30s, and the error message). Of the other audio models I could load, GLM-ASR and Qwen3-ASR handle long clips correctly and Qwen2-Audio is already fixed. I have not checked the rest.

Repro:

```python

from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams

sr = 16000
t = np.arange(sr * 35) / sr  # 35 s, longer than Whisper's 30 s window
audio = (0.1 * np.sin(2 * np.pi * 440 * t)).astype(np.float32)

llm = LLM("openai/whisper-small", max_model_len=448, limit_mm_per_prompt={"audio": 1})
out = llm.generate(
    {
        "prompt": "<|startoftranscript|><|en|><|transcribe|><|notimestamps|>",
        "multi_modal_data": {"audio": (audio, sr)},
    },
    SamplingParams(temperature=0, max_tokens=50),
)
print(out[0].outputs[0].text)
```

```bash

pytest tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_common.py -k whisper
pytest tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_tensor_schema.py -k whisper
```

The new test runs the processor on 5 s, 30 s and 35 s clips and checks that `input_features` always has the feature extractor's 3000 frames. It needs no GPU.

nodes.title: [Bugfix][Model] Mistral3: align placeholder grid with public processor
nodes.body:
## Purpose

Follow-up to #52874.

That PR fixed Mistral3 placeholder grids for processor size overrides, but the new grid calculation matches a direct call to `hf_processor.image_processor(...)`. The public `PixtralProcessor(...)` path also applies `spatial_merge_size`, so it rounds image dimensions to the merged 28-pixel stride rather than the vision encoder's 14-pixel patch size.

For dimensions that are not already aligned, vLLM can therefore still produce a different placeholder sequence from Transformers. For example:

- A 29×29 image produces 4 image tokens through the public HF processor, while current vLLM predicts 1.
- A 1540×1700 image with `longest_edge=1000` produces 1,188 image tokens through HF, while current vLLM predicts 1,152.

This change computes the grid using `patch_size * spatial_merge_size` and updates the regression test to compare the exact placeholder sequence from the public `AutoProcessor` API.

This was likely missed in #52874 because its test called the lower-level image processor directly. The test and implementation agreed with each other, but bypassed the wrapper behavior used in normal processing.

This does not duplicate an open PR; repository searches for the same Mistral3 placeholder-grid behavior returned no matches.

nodes.title: [Bugfix] Fix xgrammar feature gate bypass when JSON Schema type is a list
nodes.body:
## Purpose

JSON Schema allows `type` to be either a string or a list. Nullable type lists are also used in [OpenAI's Structured Outputs examples](https://openai.com/index/introducing-structured-outputs-in-the-api/):

```json
{"type": ["string", "null"]}
```

`has_xgrammar_unsupported_json_features` previously only recognized scalar types. As a result, schemas such as:

```json
{
  "type": ["string", "null"],
  "pattern": "^[0-9-]+$",
  "maxLength": 10
}
```

bypassed the existing unsupported-feature check. In the default `auto` mode, the request stayed on xgrammar, whose compiled grammar can accept strings longer than `maxLength`.

This PR normalizes scalar and list-valued types before applying the existing checks. Unsupported schemas now fall back to another backend, while supported list-type schemas remain on xgrammar.

## Tests

- Added numeric, string, array, and object list-type regressions.
- Added supported list-type coverage.
- Verified `auto` backend fallback.
- `79 passed` with xgrammar 0.2.1, 0.2.3, and 0.2.7.

nodes.title: [Bugfix][DSV4.1] Restrict mHC overlap to full CUDA graphs
nodes.body:
## Problem and fix

DSV4.1's small-batch eager warmup selected overlap, while breakable PIECEWISE capture selected Mega mHC. That could leave Mega mHC's stream-local barriers uninitialized until capture, causing startup to fail.

Use overlap only during FULL CUDA graph capture, still bounded by the existing 16-token cutoff and hardware requirements. Eager execution/warmup and PIECEWISE execution retain native mHC dispatch (Mega mHC where supported). Eager warmup therefore initializes Mega mHC on the capture stream. FULL replay retains the captured overlap kernels without executing the Python check per token.

The selection checks actual stream capture and excludes PIECEWISE. This works with V2's existing FULL-capture context, which advertises NONE while the runner explicitly wraps the model in `torch.cuda.graph`. CUDA graph runner/context code, AMD model code, and shared model-state code are unchanged. There is no separate warmup helper or cache. Mega mHC eligibility remains centralized in its implementation module.

## Validation

nodes.title: [Model][Engram] Share host tables across co-located DP replicas by default
nodes.body:
## Purpose

`EngramConfig.dp_shared_memory` (#56512) keeps one copy of the CPU-offloaded Engram tables per node instead of one per DP replica, with no per-step Engram DP collectives, but it had to be requested by hand and failed startup whenever its requirements were not met. This PR turns it on by default wherever it can work and falls back otherwise:

- `dp_shared_memory` defaults to unset and resolves to enabled when `cpu_offload` is on, `data_parallel_size > 1` and elastic EP is off. An explicit `true` keeps the existing strict validation.
- Before the layers are built, `can_share_engram_tables` falls back to the existing DP head sharding (same host footprint, one table per node) when the node-local Engram DP group has size 1 (replicas not co-located) or `/dev/shm` is smaller than the full tables: 188.8 GiB for DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, against Docker's default 64 MiB. Both cases log a `warning_once` pointing at `--shm-size` / `--ipc=host`. The check compares against the tmpfs total, which is identical on every rank of a node, so no collective is needed to keep the decision consistent.
- The `load_format` allowlist is dropped: `dummy` (`fill_`) and `sharded_state` (`copy_`) write identical bytes into the shared mapping on every rank, so the restriction guarded nothing.

Duplicate-work check (2026-09-19): [#57195](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57195) shares host lookups for SP token owners, [#56757](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/56757) backs tables with disk files, [#57491](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57491) keeps tables in host memory on ROCm. None changes the `dp_shared_memory` default or adds a `/dev/shm` fallback.

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (`dba1be0a`), one GB200 node, DEP4 (TP1 x DP4, EP), DSpark 5 tokens with adaptive verification, **no `--engram-config` flag**. GSM8K 5-shot via MQA, completions API, `temperature=0`, `max_tokens=1024`, n=1319.

nodes.title: [AuxOutput] Add block-keyed storage for routed-expert outputs
nodes.body:
# AuxOutput Connector: block-keyed storage for routed-expert outputs

## Summary

This PR introduces the first **AuxOutput Connector** implementation for vLLM.
The first supported auxiliary output is routed-expert output (R3): the expert IDs selected for
every token executed by an MoE model.

R3 cannot remain a request-local GPU buffer when prefix caching and async
scheduling are enabled:

- a prefix-cache hit skips model execution, so cached tokens produce no new R3;
- physical GPU/KV slots are reused and are not stable object identities;
- speculative decoding can execute rows that are later rejected;
- one result may contain cached blocks, new blocks, and a partial tail.

The connector stores immutable R3 blocks using KV-compatible block hashes. KV
and R3 for the same prefix can therefore be reused together. This PR provides a
bounded local SHM backend; distributed storage and more auxiliary output types are
follow-ups.

## Why an AuxOutput Connector?

The model capture hook only obtains a tensor from the current forward pass. A
separate lifecycle layer must decide:

- which logical tokens are accepted;
- which blocks are reusable across requests;
- when temporary GPU/CPU buffers can be released;
- where immutable blocks are stored; and
- how cached and new blocks form one ordered result.

These responsibilities also apply to future DSA and logprobs auxiliary outputs. The
connector keeps them out of the model runner and gives storage backends one
common object lifecycle. It is not a second KV Connector or a generic Scheduler
sidecar.

## Architecture

```text
+-------------------------------------------------------------------+
| API / OutputProcessor                                             |
| Current: return complete R3                                       |
| Follow-up: return ordered auxiliary output keys                           |
+-------------------------------+-----------------------------------+
                                |
                                v
+-------------------------------------------------------------------+
| EngineCore                                                        |
| Scheduler -> AuxOutputSchedulerConnector                           |
|              - logical request progress                           |
|              - KV-compatible hashes                              |
|              - terminal events                                   |
+-------------------------------+-----------------------------------+
                                | per-step metadata
                                v
+-------------------------------------------------------------------+
| GPU Worker                                                        |
| Model Runner -> router capture -> async GPU-to-CPU copy            |
|              -> AuxOutputWorkerConnector                           |
|                 - accepted-row assembly                           |
|                 - block publication/materialization               |
+-------------------------------+-----------------------------------+
                                |
                  +-------------+-------------+
                  |                           |
                  v                           v
     +--------------------------+  +--------------------------+
     | Current                  |  | Follow-up                |
     | Bounded local SHM        |  | Mooncake distributed     |
     | background publication   |  | immutable objects        |
     +--------------------------+  +--------------------------+
```

The Scheduler connector owns logical progress and hashes, not payloads. The
Worker connector owns accepted R3 rows and publication. `BlockObjectStore` owns opaque
immutable blocks and retention, but knows nothing about tokens or speculative
decoding.

## Auxiliary output types

An execution auxiliary output is an auxiliary model output that is aligned to a stable
logical coordinate and may need to outlive the worker step that produced it.

| Auxiliary output | Coordinate | Reuse | Status |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Routed experts (R3) | Executed token | Prefix block | This PR |
| DSA routing/index data | Executed token | Prefix block | Follow-up |
| Logprobs/prompt logprobs | Predicted token | Prefix block | Follow-up |
| Multimodal auxiliary data | Request/object | Request only | Exploratory |
| Sampling candidate IDs | Sampling step | Request only | Exploratory |

Prefix-block auxiliary outputs are content-addressed and reusable with a matching
prefix. Request-only auxiliary outputs use the same storage contract but do not
participate in prefix hits. Reward values, tool results, finish reasons, and
Scheduler status remain normal request/control-plane metadata.

## Current PR scope

This PR implements:

- Model Runner V2 R3 capture;
- block-keyed SHM publication and prefix materialization;
- async scheduling, chunked prefill, speculative rejection, and preemption;
- background publication, bounded capacity, and KV-aligned retention;
- terminal-only R3 delivery for streaming output;
- fail-closed checks for unsupported configurations.

It does not implement Mooncake, public auxiliary output keys, additional auxiliary output
fields, PD disaggregation, or new parallel topologies.

When disabled, no auxiliary output capture buffer, Store, per-step metadata, or R3 copy
is created on the normal serving path.

The existing `--enable-return-routed-experts` flag and `routed_experts` response
field are unchanged. The new optional configuration is exposed as
`--aux-output-config` (`AuxOutputConfig` in Python).

## Follow-ups

```text
This PR
  R3 lifecycle + local SHM
        |
        v
Unified object/profile contract + ordered keys
        |
        v
Direct Mooncake backend
        |
        v
Joint KV + mandatory-auxiliary output prefix readiness
        |
        v
DSA, logprobs, and additional topology support
```

The main planned work is:

1. define a backend-independent object/profile contract and ordered key output;
2. add a direct Mooncake backend for external trainer/JAX consumers;
3. admit remote prefix hits only when KV and mandatory auxiliary outputs are ready;
4. add DSA and logprobs through small field adapters, not new lifecycle code;
5. validate CPU KV offload, PD, PP/DCP/PCP, and multi-writer deployments before
   enabling them.

## Validation

Naming-update validation: **96 passed, 1 skipped** across configuration, store,
capture, Scheduler, output, and Ray tests. An AST comparison verified that all
24 renamed files preserve the original logic, allowing renamed identifiers,
messages, and sorted imports. Additional smoke checks passed for the existing
R3 flag, the new JSON/Python configuration, compilation hashes, serialization,
object keys, and R3 bytes. The latest naming-only update was also exercised on GB200; results and
limitations are below.

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  tests/config/test_aux_output_config.py \
  tests/distributed/aux_output_connector/test_store.py \
  tests/model_executor/test_routed_experts_capture.py \
  tests/v1/executor/test_ray_utils.py tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py \
  tests/v1/core/test_async_scheduler.py tests/v1/engine/test_output_processor.py \
  -k 'aux_output or routed_experts or pending_output or store or worker or detach_zero_copy'
pre-commit run
```

### GB200 rename A/B (2026-09-08)

Compared `85f100032e` (before rename) with `f99d53b521` (after rename) on the
same two GB200 nodes (8 GPUs), using the locally cached DeepSeek-V4-Flash-Base
FP8 weights. Both arms enable R3, MRV2, MP, TP1/DP8/EP8, async scheduling and
prefix caching. They use identical native libraries/dependencies; Python source
injection was verified by per-file SHA checks.

Workload: 64 concurrent requests, each with 262,144 input tokens and one output
token; synthetic token IDs, with output constrained to token 42. GPU memory
utilization is 0.90, max batched tokens 16,384, block size 256, and batch-invariant
mode is off. This is a serving/R3 regression test, not a model-quality evaluation.

| Measurement | Before rename | After rename |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Total throughput (input + output tokens/s) | 82,741.42 | 82,568.30 |
| Total duration | 202.768 s | 203.193 s |
| Preemptions | 0 | 0 |
| Prefix-hit tokens in the timed workload | 0 | 0 |

Throughput changed by **−0.21%** in this single A/B: no obvious regression, not a
statistical significance claim. Startup and warmup are excluded. Both arms still
reported the same first-long-request `CombineTopkSwaIndicesKernel.kernel` JIT
warning, so this is not a strictly all-kernels-warm measurement.

Correctness checks:

- All 128 long responses passed token-count, R3 row-count, shape and dtype checks.
- Separate cold/hot tests cover eight 1K-prompt/16-decode requests and eight
  64K-prompt/1-decode requests per version. The latter exercises multi-step
  chunked prefill. All requests' reused-prefix R3 SHA hashes match exactly:
  768 rows/request for the short case and 65,280 rows/request for the long case.
- All eight short cold requests have identical full R3 hashes across versions.

**Limitation: long-context full-output bitwise equivalence did not pass.** None
of the 64 full 256K R3 hashes matched across the two server runs. In the saved
request-0 sample, differences begin at row index 2051 and affect 55.38% of
elements. The same candidate version also differs when comparing the identical
first 64K input prefix in 256K versus 64K cold requests (first difference at
2051; 46.44% of elements). Recomputed decode R3 can differ between cold/hot runs
as well, already before the rename. These observations do not establish the
underlying cause or prove long-output equivalence; they must not be presented
as a full R3 correctness pass.

This run validates the response structure, exact cached-block reuse and short
cross-version outputs. It does not add new forced-preemption, speculative
decoding or free-generation quality coverage. Slurm job `24176` completed with
exit code 0; test containers and node allocations were released.

Development validation covers focused unit tests, async scheduling, forced
preemption, chunked prefill, speculative rejection, cold/hot prefix reuse,
streaming aggregation, SHM capacity/LRU behavior, pre-commit, and GB200/H200
throughput experiments reported in the PR discussion.

The latest update also moves R3 GPU-to-CPU transfer onto the existing async
output copy stream, avoiding a synchronous copy on the model execution critical
path.

AI assistance was used for implementation, testing, performance experiments,
and review. The submitting human reviewed the accepted changes and validation.

nodes.title: [Bugfix][ROCm][DSv4.1] Disable SWA bounded replay on ROCm
nodes.body:
## Purpose

Disable SWA bounded replay on ROCm, where it currently faults the GPU.

SWA bounded replay (#56227, on by default) keeps the sliding-window KV out of prefix caching and rebuilds it after a prefix hit by padding the replayed tokens' slots in the prefix-cacheable groups. Correctness depends on the consuming prefill kernel clamping the window; that clamp landed in the FlashInfer and FlashMLA paths.

The ROCm sparse SWA metadata builders (`DeepseekV4ROCMAiterSparseSWAMetadataBuilder` in both `deepseek_v4/amd/rocm.py` and `deepseek_v41/amd/rocm.py`) only gained the `replay_start` kwarg and forward it to the base builder. Nothing on the ROCm prefill path clamps the window, so the first prefix hit that carries a replay start walks off the padded slots and raises `HSA_STATUS_ERROR_MEMORY_FAULT`, which takes down the worker and then the engine core:

```
Memory access fault by GPU node-6 (Agent handle: 0x5621a810) on address 0x7ba8c13ff000. Reason: Unknown.
RuntimeError: Worker failed with error 'CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered'
RuntimeError: Engine core process EngineCore died unexpectedly.
```

This adds a ROCm guard alongside the existing model-runner-V2 and prefill-context-parallel guards in `DeepseekV4Attention`. Prefix caching itself is unaffected — the sliding-window cache simply takes part in it again, which is the pre-#56227 behavior. The guard should be removed once the ROCm prefill kernels clamp the window too.

## Test Plan

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on MI355X (gfx950), ROCm 10.0, torch 2.12.0+rocm10.0.0, Triton 3.8.0, TP=4, `--max-model-len 1048576`, `--max-num-batched-tokens 16384`, DSpark speculative decoding, `--moe-backend aiter`.

Single prompt per request at `max_tokens=1`, sweeping input length across the prefill-chunk boundary:

```
vllm serve deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
    --language-model-only --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 \
    --moe-backend aiter --gpu-memory-utilization 0.9 \
    --max-model-len 1048576 --max-num-batched-tokens 16384 \
    --speculative-config '{"method":"dspark","num_speculative_tokens":5,...}'
```

## Test Result

Baseline (`swa_bounded_replay` on, the current default):

| Input tokens | Result |
| --- | --- |
| 4,096 | OK |
| 32,768 | `HSA_STATUS_ERROR_MEMORY_FAULT`, engine core dies |

A prompt that fits in one prefill chunk passes; the fault appears once the prompt spans more than one chunk. Every fault immediately follows the first launch of `_pad_replayed_slots_kernel`. Setting `AMD_SERIALIZE_KERNEL=3` makes the same 32,768-token request pass, which is consistent with reading past the padded slots rather than with a bad constant. `TRITON_HIP_USE_ASYNC_COPY=0` only moves the threshold (32,768 passes, 131,072 still faults), so this is not a Triton async-copy issue.

With this change, on the same build and the same four GPUs:

| Input tokens | Result |
| --- | --- |
| 32,768 | OK (1.4s) |
| 131,072 | OK (5.5s) |
| 262,144 | OK (10.4s) |
| 314,510 | OK (4.3s) |

Zero memory faults, and `_pad_replayed_slots_kernel` is never launched.

End to end, a 16-configuration MI355X AgentX sweep (TP=2 and TP=4, concurrency 1-128) failed every point before this change and runs clean after it, with the accuracy arm reporting gsm8k `em_strict` 0.9750 / `em_flexible` 0.9742 over 1319 effective samples.

No new test is added: the two sibling guards in this function (model runner V2, prefill context parallelism) are likewise untested, and exercising this one requires a ROCm device with the model loaded.

nodes.title: [Security] Prefer fresh multimodal payloads over a stale receiver cache
nodes.body:
## Summary

The engine-side multimodal processor cache treated a hash hit as authoritative even when the frontend had resent a full payload. After independent LRU eviction, that lets a later request reuse the same cache identity with a different item: the engine keeps the request's placeholder layout but substitutes the stale tensor, and embedding merge then kills EngineCore. This change always stores and returns the resent payload, so a later cache-only lookup cannot revive the old item.

## Changes

- `vllm/multimodal/cache.py`: on `MultiModalReceiverCache.get_and_update_item`, if tensor data is present, drop any existing entry then cache and return that payload. Cache-only lookups (`data=None`) are unchanged, including `MultiModalCacheMissError`.
- `tests/multimodal/test_cache.py`: cover item replacement and the `get_and_update_features` engine entry.

## Codepath coverage

- Default LRU IPC cache used by EngineCore `preprocess_add_request` (`/v1/chat/completions` and other generate paths that attach `mm_features`).
- Worker SHM cache is a different class and already uses the caller's address payload rather than substituting a hash hit.
- Processor-only (no IPC) keeps prompt updates with the cached item in one process, so this drift does not apply.

## Duplicate-work check

- Open PRs searched for receiver-cache substitution, processor-cache eviction, and embedding-count mismatch.
- https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57696 rejects encoder-cache hits with mismatched embedding counts. It does not stop the processor cache from substituting a stale tensor before encode.
- https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46747 (merged) recovers the opposite drift (frontend hit, engine miss) via `MultiModalCacheMissError`. It still returns a cached item whenever the engine has a hash hit, including when a payload was resent.

## Tests

- `test_receiver_cache_replaces_stale_item_when_payload_resent`: resent larger item replaces the cached one; a later `data=None` lookup returns the new item.
- `test_receiver_cache_features_keep_resent_payload`: same control through `get_and_update_features`.

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/multimodal/test_cache.py -v -k "receiver_cache_replaces or receiver_cache_features or mm_cache_miss or oversized"
```

Passed: `test_oversized_item_is_served_uncached`, `test_mm_cache_miss_raises_and_recovers`, `test_receiver_cache_replaces_stale_item_when_payload_resent`, `test_receiver_cache_features_keep_resent_payload`, `test_mm_cache_miss_batches_all_drifted_hashes`.

nodes.title: [Bugfix][Multimodal] Tolerate malformed EXIF in Molmo 2 image preprocessing
nodes.body:
## Purpose

Follow-up to #56576 (issue #56527), which made `MultiModalHasher` tolerate a
malformed EXIF header. Molmo 2 keeps its own copy of the EXIF normalization and
that copy is **not** tolerant, so for that model the merged fix moved the
failure one step later instead of removing it.

`vllm/multimodal/image.py` suppresses the read:

```python
def normalize_image(image: Image.Image) -> Image.Image:
    """Normalize EXIF orientation so the pixel data matches visual display."""
    with contextlib.suppress(Exception):
        image = ImageOps.exif_transpose(image)
    return image
```

`vllm/model_executor/models/molmo2.py` does not:

```python
def exif_transpose(images: ImageInput | None) -> ImageInput | None:
    ...
    elif images is not None and isinstance(images, Image):
        images = ImageOps.exif_transpose(images)   # bare
    return images
```

The fix reuses `normalize_image` rather than adding a second
`contextlib.suppress`, so there is only one place that decides how a bad EXIF
block is handled. `vllm/multimodal/parse.py` already imports it the same way.

## Why the second read is the one that raises

This is the non-obvious part, and it is why the bug survived #56576. Measured on
Pillow 12.3.0 with the payload from #56576's test:

| sequence | result |
| --- | --- |
| `Image.open(...)` then `ImageOps.exif_transpose(im)` | no raise |
| `ImageMediaIO.load_bytes(...)` then `ImageOps.exif_transpose(im)` | `SyntaxError: not a TIFF file (header b'XXXX\x00\x00\x00\x08' not valid)` |
| the same, second call on the same object | no raise |

`ImageMediaIO.load_bytes` (`vllm/multimodal/media/image.py:90-92`) runs
`normalize_image(image)` -> `image.load()` -> `_convert_image_mode(image)`. The
suppressed transpose plus `load()` is what primes Pillow's lazy EXIF state, and
`.convert()` carries that state forward — so the *next* read raises, and only
the next one (Pillow caches the failure afterwards). That last row is why the
regression test loads a fresh image for every case; reusing one would make the
test pass on `main` by coincidence.

## Reachability

`POST /v1/chat/completions` against a Molmo 2 model with an `image_url` whose
JPEG carries a malformed APP1/Exif segment:

1. `ImageMediaIO.load_bytes` primes the EXIF state (above).
2. Hashing runs next and is now tolerant, thanks to #56576.
3. `Molmo2MultiModalProcessor._get_prompt_updates` ->
   `get_image_replacement_molmo2` (`molmo2.py:2218`) -> the bare
   `exif_transpose` -> `SyntaxError`.

`SyntaxError` is neither `VLLMClientError` nor `GracefulHTTPError`, so
`AsyncLLM.generate`'s generic handler wraps it as
`raise EngineGenerateError() from e` (`vllm/v1/engine/async_llm.py:764`) — a 500
with an empty `message`, matching what #56527 reported for the hasher.

## Is the class fully fixed?

Yes. `grep -rn "exif_transpose\|getexif" --include=*.py vllm/` on current `main`
returns four sites:

| site | state |
| --- | --- |
| `vllm/multimodal/image.py:24` | suppressed |
| `vllm/multimodal/hasher.py:74` | tolerant since #56576 |
| `vllm/model_executor/models/molmo2.py:1302` | **fixed here** |
| `vllm/model_executor/models/molmo2.py:1299` | recursive call into the same function |

Molmo 2 was the only remaining bare read, so no follow-up is needed.

## Test

**No test ships with this PR** — removed at the reviewer's request
(review of 2026-09-17: "Thanks but let's remove the tests"). The diff is now
the two-line source change only.

For the record, the regression test that had been in this PR was verified on
**fork CI run
[35144842256](https://github.com/Hotragn/vllm/actions/runs/35144842256)**, with
BEFORE run against `main` (`30b847c1fa`):

BEFORE — **1 failed**, and the failure is the defect itself rather than an
incidental assertion:

```
tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_molmo2.py:135: in test_exif_transpose_tolerates_malformed_exif
    assert exif_transpose(_served_image()) is not None
vllm/model_executor/models/molmo2.py:1302: in exif_transpose
    images = ImageOps.exif_transpose(images)
PIL/ImageOps.py:703: in exif_transpose
    image_exif = image.getexif()
...
E  SyntaxError: not a TIFF file (header b'XXXX' not valid)
```

AFTER — the whole file: **6 passed**. Whole-suite
`pytest tests/models/multimodal/processing` on both sides: the same two
pre-existing collection errors (`test_llava_next.py`, `test_llava_onevision.py`),
identical on `main` and on the branch.

Local lint on the remaining change, all clean: `ruff check` / `ruff format`
(0.14.0), `typos` (1.43.5), `check_spdx_header`, `check_forbidden_imports`,
`check_torch_cuda`, `check_init_lazy_imports`.

pytest cannot run on my local machine (Windows-on-ARM), hence the fork runner;
the Pillow measurements in the table above were made locally with Pillow alone.

## Notes

AI assistance was used to research and draft this change. I have reviewed every
changed line and verified the change as described above.

## Purpose

PR3 for RFC #47161, following #47301 and #50550. Adds streaming parity CI and docs for the streaming derender endpoints.

**Parity tests.** `test_derender_parity.py` now covers `stream=true`. It streams `/v1/chat/completions` with `return_token_ids=True` and sends each chunk's tokens through the chunked `/v1/chat/completions/derender` with the same boundaries. The assembled content, reasoning, tool calls and `finish_reason` have to match. Tool call IDs compare by format and neither side may change an ID mid stream.

Cases are plain, reasoning, auto tool call and reasoning + forced tool call. The last one also runs with multi-token chunks (`stream_interval=4`, shaped like spec decode) and with the finish reason on a trailing chunk with no tokens. Derender gets the engine's finish reason rather than the chat one, so the `tool_calls` rewrite is tested.

The stream helpers in `test_derender_stream.py` move to a shared `utils.py` so both files use them.

**Docs.** `derenderer.md` gets the streaming request formats, the client loop contract (echo `stream_state`, one choice per chunk, `n > 1` as N streams, forward the usage chunk) and a streaming example. It also notes that streaming drops
logprobs for now. It picks up the two docs items from #42729 too: the render server's parser and chat template flags have to match `vllm serve` and completions don't parse. `protocol.py` only gains snippet markers.

**Not in this PR.** The batch parity test still feeds the coupled `finish_reason` into derender. Fixing that and checking batch tool call ID format would fail on `main` until #47931 and the batch tool call ID fix land, so it follows them. The
logprobs line in the docs changes when #55029 lands.

**Why the tool cases look the way they do.** In #50550's CI run, batch `test_parity_tool_call` was skipped because the model hit `max_tokens` inside the `<tool_call>` JSON. Streamed tool call arguments can be partial JSON, so they compare as raw strings. The streaming tool cases use `max_tokens=512` because replay is O(n³).
