nodes.title: [Pooling] Fix normalization of chunked long-text embeddings
nodes.body:
## Purpose

Averaging normalized chunks can produce a non-unit long-text embedding. Re-normalize multi-chunk aggregates when `use_activation=True`, preserving single-chunk and raw outputs.

## Reproducer

The temporary CPU reproducer passes two equal-weight, orthogonal normalized
chunk embeddings through `_post_process_chunked`. It also checks a one-chunk
BF16 prompt and the `use_activation=False` path.

```bash
env PYTHONPATH=<main-worktree> .venv/bin/python /tmp/chunked_norm_cpu_reproducer.py
env PYTHONPATH=$PWD .venv/bin/python /tmp/chunked_norm_cpu_reproducer.py
```

## Output on main / on branch

Main:

```text
multi=[0.5, 0.5] norm=0.707107
single_exact=True value=[0.6015625, 0.80078125]
raw=[0.5, 0.5]
```

Branch:

```text
multi=[0.7071067690849304, 0.7071067690849304] norm=1.000000
single_exact=True value=[0.6015625, 0.80078125]
raw=[0.5, 0.5]
```

## H100 multi-model evaluation

The  end-to-end sweep used BF16, `max_model_len=128`, and long inputs of 1,192-1,682 tokens. It covered encoder mean pooling, encoder CLS pooling, and decoder last-token pooling.

| Model | Architecture / pooling | Old multi-chunk norms | New multi-chunk norms | Short max abs delta across independent servers | Minimum cosine with old output | Retrieval ranking |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| `intfloat/e5-small-v2` | encoder / MEAN | 0.997116-0.997419 | 1.000000 | 7.45e-9 | 1.000000 | cosine and IP unchanged |
| `BAAI/bge-small-en-v1.5` | encoder / CLS | 0.986880-0.993246 | 1.000000 | 1.49e-8 | 1.000000 | cosine and IP unchanged |
| `Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B` | decoder / LAST | 0.784638-0.821176 | 1.000000 | 7.45e-9 | 0.999994 | cosine unchanged; IP changed |

For E5 and BGE, the new long output matched an explicitly normalized old weighted mean within `2.98e-8`. Qwen's maximum BF16 difference was `4.73e-4` with the same cosine ranking. Its IP ranking changed from `[0, 1, 2, 4, 3]`
to `[0, 1, 4, 2, 3]`, demonstrating why this should be documented as an intentional correctness-related output change rather than a refactor.

Short prompts do not execute the new normalization operation. The direct BF16 aggregation check is bitwise exact; independent H100 server launches differed by at most `1.49e-8`, consistent with normal numerical variation.

### Compatibility note

Only normalized outputs formed from multiple chunks change. Their direction is preserved while their magnitude becomes approximately 1. Cosine retrieval is therefore expected to remain stable, but inner-product scores and rankings can change. Deployments using inner-product indexes should not mix old and new long-document embeddings; re-embed affected long documents when upgrading.

## Test plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/entrypoints/pooling/embed/test_io_processor.py -q
# 46 passed

env UV_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/vllm-uv-cache .venv/bin/pre-commit run \
  --files vllm/entrypoints/pooling/embed/io_processor.py
# Passed

env UV_CACHE_DIR=/tmp/vllm-uv-cache .venv/bin/pre-commit run \
  --all-files --hook-stage manual
# Passed, including dependency locks and mypy for Python 3.10-3.13
```

The deterministic temporary CPU reproducer and the three-model H100 E2E sweep also passed with the outputs summarized above.


## AI assistance disclosure

OpenAI Codex (GPT-5) assisted with drafting the implementation and temporary validation scripts.

nodes.title: [ROCm][DSv4] Enable DSpark adaptive verification
nodes.body: ## Purpose Enable DSpark confidence-scheduled adaptive verification for DeepSeek-V4 on ROCm. Developed with contributions from [@larryli2-amd](https://github.com/larryli2-amd), who added explicit missing-confidence-head error handling and provided the MI350X performance validation. This change: - adds AMD confidence-head construction, inference, checkpoint remapping, and safe fallback when a checkpoint has no confidence head - enables variable-length FULL graph support in the DeepSeek-V4 ROCm sparse MLA and sparse SWA metadata builders when adaptive verification is enabled, while retaining their existing support classification otherwise - extends the shared DeepSeek indexer flattening capability to the ROCm DeepSeek-V4 path, deriving adaptive request ownership from device query boundaries - adds focused confidence-loading and graph-replay regression coverage Adaptive verification can redistribute a fixed draft-token budget between requests on device, so CPU request boundaries can differ from final device boundaries. The flattened path builds request ownership, context lengths, and block-table rows from device decode lengths. It reuses the shared flattening selection introduced by [#52795](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52795) and keeps the ROCm capability scoped to the DeepSeek-V4 builder. NVIDIA and unrelated ROCm indexers are unchanged. The ROCm sparse MLA/SWA declarations are similarly scoped. Their ragged metadata is device-boundary-derived and copied into persistent buffers before FULL graph replay. AI assistance was used in preparing this PR. ## Test plan - changed-file pre-commit, including Ruff and mypy for Python 3.10–3.13; - focused AMD confidence-head, ROCm adaptive metadata, native `next_n`, and adaptive-verification tests; - complete GSM8K 5-shot evaluation for no speculation, fixed K=7, and adaptive K<=7; - SPEED-Bench throughput comparison on 8x MI350X at TP=8 and client concurrency 4/8/16/32/64/128/256. - Rocm vllm nightly ShareGPT throughput comparison on 8x MI355X at TP=8 and client concurrency 4/8/16/32/64/128/256. ## Test results ### Source and focused tests - rebased PR head `ea586873d5210d9e1624c42333be1b02c276c832` onto upstream `cd10ed6f9f6b37a8ace9cf380007e66fe12ec0c3`; - changed-file pre-commit passed, including Ruff and mypy for Python 3.10–3.13; - the two PR-specific test files passed (`10 passed`) and the shared adaptive-verification suite passed (`13 passed`). ### Performance validation — 8x MI350X Performance validation contributed by [@larryli2-amd](https://github.com/larryli2-amd) used 8x AMD Instinct MI350X at TP=8 with `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-DSpark`. This PR changes only vLLM; it does not modify or vendor AITER source code. The benchmark environment used a locally rebuilt, pinned AITER wheel installed into the derived image with `--no-deps`, leaving the base PyTorch and Triton installations unchanged: - base image: `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm@sha256:72e90adf360ccffb231a098a15eadfb808719c029c6cd43f6386095064552b7e`; - AITER version: `0.1.21.post2.dev2+g804648bcb`; - AITER source: `804648bcbf87646ddef4b7add10da9c3b322567c`; - AITER wheel SHA256: `30360d15819a9c8e3ec8e4ae665683abf4c5358d5be1f49a9aa2f7962c0032db`; - PyTorch: `2.12.0+rocm10.0.0`. The pinned wheel was used because the stock AITER post1 environment had a known GPU-fault issue in this setup. The server used Model Runner V2, breakable CUDA graphs, async scheduling, prefix caching, FP8 KV cache, `max_num_seqs=256`, `max_num_batched_tokens=16384`, and `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` capture through 2048. Adaptive DSpark used K<=7 and an 8192-token profiling context. The benchmark used a frozen 880-request SPEED-Bench Throughput-1K request set at temperature 1, top-p 1, and maximum output length 2048. Concurrency ran in descending order from 256 to 4. Each point used an independent cold server boot, two 64-request warmups, matching client/server generated-token counts, zero preemptions, and no GPU faults. Compared with fixed-length verification, confidence-scheduled DSpark delivered comparable performance at low concurrency and higher throughput at high concurrency. The complete serving command and environment details are preserved in the [reproduction comment](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52362#issuecomment-5675603735). ### ROCm nightly validation — 8x MI355X The main rerun used upstream `cd10ed6f9f6b37a8ace9cf380007e66fe12ec0c3`, PR head `ea586873d5210d9e1624c42333be1b02c276c832`, and stock-AITER image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-cd10ed6f9f6b37a8ace9cf380007e66fe12ec0c3`. The server used TP=8, FP8 KV, `max_num_seqs=256`, `max_num_batched_tokens=4096`, `max_model_len=4096`, synchronous scheduling, prefix caching disabled, and `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` capture through 2048. Both DSpark arms used probabilistic sampling. `AITER_USE_CK_MOE_SORTING=1` avoids a stock AITER post1 sorting fault; AITER MLA/OPUS remained enabled. ShareGPT output throughput, tokens/s: | Concurrency | No speculation | Fixed K=7 | Adaptive K<=7 | Adaptive vs fixed K=7 | Adaptive vs no-spec | |---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 4 | 381.53 | 970.33 | 902.37 | -7.00% | +136.51% | | 8 | 729.20 | 1,762.59 | 1,616.77 | -8.27% | +121.72% | | 16 | 1,342.83 | 2,909.52 | 2,773.69 | -4.67% | +106.56% | | 32 | 2,392.99 | 4,756.32 | 4,501.11 | -5.37% | +88.10% | | 64 | 4,094.75 | 6,712.35 | 7,144.12 | +6.43% | +74.47% | | 128 | 6,340.78 | 8,778.87 | 10,356.48 | +17.97% | +63.33% | | 256 | 8,878.57 | 7,852.42 | 13,324.67 | +69.69% | +50.08% | Each cell used a fresh server, one readiness request, a 64-request c32 warmup, a 64-request cell-concurrency warmup, and 880 measured raw-ShareGPT requests with forced output length 512. All 21 cells completed 880/880 requests with the expected 450,560 generated tokens, no preemptions, and no GPU faults. The complete three-arm, 1,319-sample GSM8K 5-shot gate also passed: | Mode | Flexible exact match | Strict exact match | |---|---:|---:| | No speculation | `0.9484 +/- 0.0061` | `0.9484 +/- 0.0061` | | Fixed K=7 | `0.9431 +/- 0.0064` | `0.9431 +/- 0.0064` | | Adaptive K<=7 | `0.9492 +/- 0.0060` | `0.9492 +/- 0.0060` | The score range was `0.0061`, within one reported standard error. For each concurrency, start a fresh server, run the two 64-request warmups described above, then run: ```bash vllm bench serve \ --backend vllm \ --dataset-name sharegpt \ --dataset-path "$SHAREGPT_PATH" \ --disable-shuffle \ --ignore-eos \ --request-rate inf \ --max-concurrency "$CONCURRENCY" \ --num-prompts 880 \ --sharegpt-output-len 512 \ --temperature 1.0 \ --seed 20260902 \ --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 \ --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v4 \ --trust-remote-code ``` The GSM8K gate used: ```bash lm_eval \ --model local-completions \ --model_args model=deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731,base_url=http://localhost:8000/v1/completions,num_concurrent=16,tokenizer_backend=none,tokenized_requests=False \ --tasks gsm8k \ --num_fewshot 5 \ --batch_size 1 \ --seed 42 ``` ## Current ROCm qualification On current ROCm main/nightly, DeepSeek-V4 defaults to Model Runner V1, while DSpark requires Model Runner V2. nodes.title: [Bugfix] Fix external LB DP rank handling when replicas share nodes
nodes.body:
stack two fixes together
1# Fix ZeroDivisionError with external LB when DP size exceeds node count in multi-node setups
2# Fix external LB rank inference on shared nodes https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54694

## Purpose

`ParallelConfig.nnodes_within_dp` reports how many nodes a single DP replica
spans, computed as `nnodes // (data_parallel_size // data_parallel_size_local)`.

The formula assumes `data_parallel_size_local` describes DP ranks per node. That
holds for internal LB, where it is inferred — and the inference already guards
the same floor-rounding hazard (`arg_utils.py:2144`):

```python
self.data_parallel_size_local = max(local_world_size // world_size_within_dp, 1)
```

External LB instead pins it to 1 for its one-engine-per-process model
(`arg_utils.py:2183`), so the denominator becomes the full DP size and the ratio
floors to **0** whenever replicas outnumber nodes.

## Where it divides by zero

Two properties in `ParallelConfig` use the value as a divisor:

```python
# vllm/config/parallel.py:742
def node_rank_within_dp(self) -> int:
    return self.node_rank % self.nnodes_within_dp

# vllm/config/parallel.py:755
def local_world_size(self) -> int:
    return self.world_size // self.nnodes_within_dp
```

`MultiprocExecutor._get_parallel_sizes` reaches both before any worker is
spawned (`vllm/v1/executor/multiproc_executor.py:279`):

```python
assert self.world_size % self.parallel_config.nnodes_within_dp == 0, (...)
self.local_world_size = self.parallel_config.local_world_size
```

The assert raises `ZeroDivisionError` rather than `AssertionError`; under
`python -O` it is stripped and the next line raises instead. Startup aborts in
the executor, before `Worker.init_device()` runs, so the fix belongs in
`nnodes_within_dp` itself rather than in each caller.

nodes.title: [Bugfix][NIXL] Fix DCP pulls across MLA cache regions
nodes.body:
When prefill and decode use different cache-group layouts, as with a HiSparse decoder, NIXL matches their KV blocks by memory region. That receive path currently assumes a single source rank and fails when a DCP prefiller supplies multiple ranks.

Create a read for each source rank using the existing region mapping. For each region, reuse `_apply_dcp_prefix_caching` to select the pages owned by that rank and skip the decoder's cached prefix. Bound the reads by the sequence length and zero any remaining allocation padding. The ordinary DCP path stays unchanged. Requires unshared MLA regions with matching logical/kernel page sizes.

Independent of #55398's GPU-landing feature; #57077 covers DCP1 only.


Controlled PowerMoE and HyperCLOVAX comparisons reduced peak RSS from 20.26 to 15.96 GiB and 83.74 to 58.80 GiB while preserving generated outputs, sampled weights, and device placement. nodes.title: [ROCm][Perf] Route the fused shared-expert gate GEMM through the platform dispatcher
nodes.body:
## Purpose

When `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS` is on, `MoERunner` concatenates the router gate and the shared-expert gate into a single `[num_experts + num_shared, hidden]` weight and computes the combined logits with a bare `F.linear`. The un-fused `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=0` branch immediately below it calls `self.gate(hidden_states)`, a `ReplicatedLinear` whose `UnquantizedLinearMethod.apply` goes through `dispatch_unquantized_gemm()`.

The problem is that FSE silently replaced ROCm's skinny-GEMM kernels with Tensile `Cijk_*` kernels firing once per MoE layer
per decode step. Those kernels cost 110.6 ms per 100 decode steps where the skinny path does the same GEMM in 55.6 ms, a nearly 2x regression on this GEMM.

This PR routes the fused path through `dispatch_unquantized_gemm()` as well.
* On ROCm that reaches `rocm_unquantized_gemm`, matching the un-fused path; 
* On every other platform `dispatch_unquantized_gemm()` returns `F.linear`, so the change is a no-op there.


Beyond the immediate win, this also puts the fused gate back onto the path that can reach AITER's tuned GEMM at all. `F.linear` goes straight to rocBLAS and never consults AITER for tuned kernels. After this change the GEMMs flow through `rocm_unquantized_gemm_impl` into `aiter.tuned_gemm.mm`, and any tuned configuration AITER ships for this shape is picked up automatically with no further vLLM change.


## Test Plan

Models
* `amd/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-Quark-MXFP4` -> `Quark-MXFP4`: publicly available, for baseline 
* `amd/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-MoE-MXFP4` -> `MoE-MXFP4`: custom checkpoint enabling FP4-quantized fused shared experts

All runs on MI355X (gfx950), TP8, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`, AITER attention, `--ignore-eos`, identical seeds on both arms; the arms differ only by this patch.

**Kernel-level.** PyTorch profiler traces over a decode-only window, comparing per-kernel time before and after.

**Serving throughput and latency.** 

| ISL | OSL | Max concurrency | Prompts |
|-----|-----|-----------------|---------|
| 1024 | 1024 | 4 | 32 |
| 1024 | 1024 | 8 | 64 |
| 1024 | 1024 | 16 | 96 |
| 1024 | 1024 | 32 | 128 |
| 1024 | 1024 | 128 | 384 |

**Accuracy.** GSM8K, 5-shot, three arms -- `Quark-MXFP4` with FSE off, `MoE-MXFP4` with FSE off, `MoE-MXFP4` with FSE on -- to keep the checkpoint change separate from the fused-shared-experts change.

## Test Result

### Kernels

Decode-only trace at conc=4; ms per 100 decode steps:

| Arm | Total | wvSplitK | Tensile `Cijk_*` |
|-----|-------|----------|------------------|
| Fused shared experts off | 1807.5 | 330.4 | 0.0 |
| Fused shared experts on, before this PR | 1419.8 | 275.2 | 110.6 |
| Fused shared experts on, with this PR | 1368.9 | 330.8 | 0.0 |

The `Cijk_*` kernels disappear and total wvSplitK time returns to the un-fused level (330.8 against 330.4), which confirms the fused 513-wide gate is no more expensive than the 512-wide router gate it replaces. Net recovery is about 51 ms per 100 decode steps.

### Serving benchmarks

Median of three runs per case for the patched arm, one run per case for the baseline. Each cell is `before → after (change)`; higher is better for throughput, lower for latency.

| ISL | OSL | Conc | Prompts | Output tok/s | Mean TTFT (ms) | Mean TPOT (ms) | Mean E2EL (ms) |
|-----|-----|------|---------|--------------|----------------|----------------|----------------|
| 1024 | 1024 | 4 | 32 | 279.6 → 289.4 (+3.5%) | 177.1 → 179.1 (+1.1%) | 13.78 → 13.29 (-3.5%) | 13,445.7 → 12,988.4 (-3.4%) |
| 1024 | 1024 | 8 | 64 | 414.7 → 415.6 (+0.2%) | 214.4 → 215.3 (+0.4%) | 17.74 → 17.74 (-0.0%) | 16,860.0 → 16,860.3 (+0.0%) |
| 1024 | 1024 | 16 | 96 | 687.6 → 687.5 (-0.0%) | 284.0 → 283.5 (-0.2%) | 21.02 → 21.06 (+0.2%) | 22,840.0 → 22,894.9 (+0.2%) |
| 1024 | 1024 | 32 | 128 | 976.1 → 972.5 (-0.4%) | 411.5 → 445.7 (+8.3%) | 28.17 → 28.40 (+0.8%) | 29,632.2 → 29,870.6 (+0.8%) |
| 1024 | 1024 | 128 | 384 | 2,178.8 → 2,165.4 (-0.6%) | 1,298.6 → 1,295.7 (-0.2%) | 49.72 → 50.25 (+1.1%) | 51,305.5 → 51,752.2 (+0.9%) |

Geometric mean output throughput over the five cases: **+0.5%**. 

`rocm_unquantized_gemm_impl` only selects the wvSplitK skinny kernels when the token count is at most 5. At concurrency 4 the decode batch stays inside that window, which is where the +3.5% comes from. Above it, the call falls through to `aiter.tuned_gemm.mm`, whose tuned table has no entry for the 513-wide fused gate, so the lookup misses and AITER circles back to its default `torch` solution -- the same rocBLAS kernel the previous `F.linear` used. Performance above that boundary is therefore unchanged by construction, and the flat rows are the expected result rather than a regression.

That gap is on the ROCm/AITER side, not in vLLM. Tuning the shape offline (N=513, K=8192, bf16, on gfx950) shows the fallback is leaving performance on the table at every batch size tested, at no cost in accuracy (error ratio 0.0 for every selected kernel):

| Tokens | rocBLAS fallback | Best available (hipBLASLt) | Speedup |
|--------|------------------|----------------------------|---------|
| 8 | 12.10 µs | 8.85 µs | 1.37x |
| 16 | 11.63 µs | 8.75 µs | 1.33x |
| 64 | 12.53 µs | 11.08 µs | 1.13x |
| 256 | 15.36 µs | 14.28 µs | 1.07x |
| 1024 | 28.86 µs | 23.25 µs | 1.24x |
| 8192 | 108.18 µs | 89.66 µs | 1.21x |

Closing that gap belongs in AITER, as tuned configurations for the fused gate width and, potentially, relaxed shape constraints. This PR is the prerequisite for any of it reaching the fused path: as long as the gate went through `F.linear`, AITER was never consulted for this GEMM at all. Once those configurations land, the fused gate picks them up with no further vLLM changes.

### GSM8K

5-shot, 1319 problems, `lm_eval` with `tensor_parallel_size=8`, `max_gen_toks=2048`, seed 4321.

| Arm | flexible-extract | strict-match |
|-----|------------------|--------------|
| Quark-MXFP4, fused shared experts off | 0.9318 ± 0.0069 | 0.9333 ± 0.0069 |
| MoE-MXFP4, fused shared experts off | 0.9310 ± 0.0070 | 0.9318 ± 0.0069 |
| MoE-MXFP4, fused shared experts on | 0.9280 ± 0.0071 | 0.9280 ± 0.0071 |
| MoE-MXFP4, fused shared experts on, with this PR | 0.9227 ± 0.0074 | 0.9219 ± 0.0074 |

All four arms are statistically indistinguishable; the widest gap, between the Quark-MXFP4 reference and this PR, is 1.1 standard errors of the difference. The second arm isolates the checkpoint change (shared expert pre-quantized to MXFP4) from fusion itself, so the third is attributable to fusion alone, and the fourth to this patch alone.

---

nodes.title: [Engram] Drop redundant VLLM_PLE_CPU_OFFLOAD env var
nodes.body:
TL;DR the functionality of this env var should now be covered by the engram config args (similar process to attention backend and other configs flags) @ZJY0516

## Motivation

`VLLM_PLE_CPU_OFFLOAD` predates `EngramConfig`, but today it no longer enables any behavior of its own. Its only consumer in the tree was `_default_cpu_offload()` in `vllm/config/engram.py`, the `default_factory` for `EngramConfig.cpu_offload`. No runtime code read it directly: the DeepSeek V4.1 and Qwen4Exp embedding paths branch on `engram_config.cpu_offload`, never on the env var, and `VllmConfig._resolve_and_verify_engram_config` already gives an explicit `--engram-config` value precedence over the env-derived default.

In other words, `VLLM_PLE_CPU_OFFLOAD=0` was exactly equivalent to:

```
--engram-config '{"cpu_offload": false}'
```

Consistent with prior cleanups (e.g. attention backend env vars migrated into config), we want to minimize env vars since they are less discoverable, less documented, and invisible in engine configs and hashes. This PR drops the env var and makes the enabled-by-default behavior a plain field default, so `cpu_offload` is now configured solely through `EngramConfig` / `--engram-config`.


## Notes for reviewers

- Default behavior is unchanged: `cpu_offload` remains `True` when no config is passed. `VllmConfig._resolve_and_verify_engram_config` still constructs a default `EngramConfig()` for supported models on CUDA-like platforms.
- Breaking change for anyone setting `VLLM_PLE_CPU_OFFLOAD=0` in their environment: the setting is now silently ignored in favor of the default. The flag was not documented in `docs/` and only affects DeepSeek V4.1 / Qwen4Exp PLE models; the replacement is a one-line config flag.
- `dp_shared_memory` validation and the `compute_hash` path are untouched; they already operate on the config field.

## Not duplicating existing work

Checked open PRs before opening this one; related PLE offload PRs (#57497 ROCm PLE offload, #54070 disk offload) add new behavior and do not remove or standardize this env var.

## Testing

- `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` on all changed files: pass.
- Full pre-commit hook suite on the commit: all pass.
- Direct verification against the changed tree (the local sandbox venv is older than `upstream/main` and cannot import `tests/test_config.py` as a whole, so the module-level pytest run was not possible there):
  - `vllm.envs` no longer exposes `VLLM_PLE_CPU_OFFLOAD`.
  - `EngramConfig().cpu_offload is True`; explicit `cpu_offload=False` respected; `dp_shared_memory=True, cpu_offload=False` still raises `ValueError`.
  - The `--engram-config` CLI parse path (`get_kwargs(VllmConfig)["engram_config"]`) parses `{"cpu_offload": false}` into an `EngramConfig` and round-trips through `EngineArgs`.
  - CI will run `tests/test_config.py` on the updated `test_engram_cpu_offload_default`.

This PR was prepared with AI assistance; the changes were reviewed end-to-end by the submitter.

nodes.title: [Bugfix][MoE] Reject hash routing for unsupported monolithic backends
nodes.body:
- Add a per-layer `has_hash_routing` field to `FusedMoEConfig`, defaulting to false.
- Populate it from the hash table supplied to `FusedMoEFactory`.
- Reject hash-routed layers in the common capability check for all current monolithic backends, whose interface does not carry token IDs or hash tables.
- Preserve modular hash routing and ordinary non-hash monolithic selection.
- Add six factory-to-oracle cases covering monolithic AITER, native modular AITER, and modular Triton with and without hash routing.

This issue was uncovered during local MI300 reproduction of the [CI 90039 speculative-decoding group](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/90039/list?sid=01a0bd6c-73d2-48d6-82a3-1e021270e178&tab=output). The A16 DeepSeek V4 capability added in [#46516](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46516) already lacked a hash-input path, and [#50622](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50622) later made that backend available on gfx942. Modular execution selects experts using token IDs and the hash table, but current monolithic execution bypasses that router and drops the required inputs. Recording the layer requirement before backend selection prevents an otherwise eligible monolithic backend from silently using a different routing algorithm. 

Related work: [#45711](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/45711) extends the monolithic interface and implements hash routing for a new AITER MXFP8 backend. This standalone change contains none of that implementation and intentionally rejects every monolithic backend under the current interface. If that extension lands, this blanket check must be revisited to admit explicitly implemented hash capability while continuing to reject unsupported backends. [#50844](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50844) bounds token IDs in a hash-routing kernel; it addresses input validation rather than backend eligibility.

Investigation, implementation, validation, and this description were AI-assisted.

nodes.title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Reject unsupported EP for monolithic AITER MXFP4 MoE
nodes.body:
- Reject `use_ep=True` for the monolithic AITER MXFP4 W4A16 and static-FP8 W4A8 backends.
- Check expert sharding directly: `use_all2all_kernels=False` does not imply that all experts are local.
- Preserve supported tensor parallel configurations and the existing data parallel and EPLB restrictions.
- Add four capability-selection cases covering both backends with and without expert parallelism.

This issue surfaced while reproducing the [CI 90039 speculative-decoding group](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/90039/list?sid=01a0bd6c-73d2-48d6-82a3-1e021270e178&tab=output) locally on MI300. [#50622](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/50622) split the CK and Triton W4A16 backends and made the unsafe selection reachable on gfx942; a source-predicate bisect identified that change, rather than a GPU numerical bisect. With TP4 and expert parallelism enabled, the runtime observer measured 256 global routing experts but only 64 local weight experts, and the W4A16 kernel faulted after indexing those local weights with global expert IDs. Both current monolithic implementations ignore the expert map, so they must reject expert parallelism until that contract is implemented.

Related work: [#53261](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53261) fixes token-row metadata in native modular AITER, while [#45711](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/45711) introduces a new MXFP8 backend. Neither implements this EP exclusion for the two existing monolithic backends.

Investigation, implementation, validation, and this description were AI-assisted.

nodes.title: [Docker] Use zstd for CI images and offer a Docker Hub variant
nodes.body:
The ordinary CUDA CI image now exports zstd level 3 under the existing ECR commit tag that test runners consume. Standard Docker Hub tags retain their separate gzip release path, and the CUDA 13.0 amd64 release action also publishes a separately tagged `-zstd` variant from an immutable release-image digest by default. The requested test script has been removed.

The CI change applies to the ordinary `test-ci` build. CPU/Arm builds and the separate Torch-nightly builder retain their existing paths. The public release variant stays separately tagged because ordinary pulls do not provide a reliable same-tag gzip fallback for unsupported zstd consumers.

## Measurement

Earlier matched images on one RTX 4090 Laptop rig, Qwen3-0.6B, four-CPU quota, local registry and three fresh-store runs per arm:

| Image | Compressed bytes | Median pull to first correct response |
|---|---:|---:|
| Bytecode, gzip | 8,664,824,384 | 144.51 s |
| Same image, zstd level 3 | 6,999,776,144 | 118.02 s |

The zstd image is 19.2% smaller, with a 22.19-second median paired saving. Paired savings differ from subtracting the arm medians. This is the earlier same-host local-registry experiment, not a measurement of production ECR or Internet delivery.

## Validation

Merged current main and passed applicable pre-commit hooks, including ShellCheck and Buildkite configuration checks. The actual ci-infra consumers select the unchanged ECR commit tag, so no separate runner tag change is needed.

[CI build 89441](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/89441#01a0abf5-32fd-4467-8e35-6e8b54bc6ce9) exported the `69f15d2e2e0137af8d0b10a693af28e54e907fb3` image with 44 zstd layers. I then pulled Linux amd64 digest `sha256:81fe52601ccf6c61d8824016483e81fd24244491211cf4973b285fda6d4408d2` on my rig: Python 3.12.3, Torch 2.13.0+cu130 and vLLM imports passed, followed by a small CUDA matrix multiplication on the selected RTX 4090 Laptop. The temporary container/image reference were removed and the existing snapshot workload was preserved. The CI exporter and zstd export helper are unchanged by the default-publication update. Mac and Linux command-spy checks passed for all release targets and export-failure cleanup; the normal gzip calls are preserved. Repository hooks passed. nodes.title: [CI][Build] Harden triton-cpu sleef submodule fetch in CPU image build
nodes.body:
## Problem

CPU lanes on main are failing at image build (builds [#90092](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/90092), [#90127](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/90127) — all 6 CPU shards red): triton-cpu's pinned clone (270e696d) occasionally leaves `third_party/sleef` empty, and CMake dies with 'does not contain a CMakeLists.txt file'. The submodule fetch via `--shallow-submodules --filter=blob:none` flakes under network/endpoint conditions and the build has no check.

## Fix

After checkout, verify `third_party/sleef/CMakeLists.txt` exists; if not, refetch unshallow and force-update submodules. Fail fast with a clear message if it's still missing (surfacing a real upstream outage instead of an opaque CMake error).

Signed-off-by: kimi-no-na-wa <kimi-no-na-wa@users.noreply.github.com>

nodes.title: [Bugfix][Kernel] Skip the fused silu-mul block-quant fast path when a swiglu clamp is set
nodes.body:
## Purpose

The fused `silu_and_mul_per_block_quant` fast path in `TritonExperts.apply` has no clamp
parameter, so a configured SwiGLU clamp limit (`gemm1_clamp_limit`, or `swiglu_limit` from
the model config) is silently dropped for fp8 w8a8 block-[128, 128] experts. Gate that fast
path on `clamp_limit is None` so clamped models fall back to the existing
`swiglu_limit_func` path, while unclamped models keep the fusion.

- Introduced by #42497. In-tree, EXAONE MoE reaches this path: it passes
  `activation="silu"` with a per-layer `swiglu_limit`.
- `TritonExperts` is selected whenever `TritonOrDeepGemmExperts` rejects DeepGEMM, so
  exposure depends on shape and environment: small `M`, small `N`, non-contiguous weights,
  or DeepGEMM not installed, in which case every shape is affected.
  `VLLM_USE_DEEP_GEMM_E8M0=1` also masks the bug via the existing
  `not is_deep_gemm_e8m0_used()` term in the same condition.
- `CutlassExperts` already gates its own fused SiLU+quant fast path on
  `activation_config.clamp_limit is None`, so this follows existing precedent.
- `DeepGemmExperts`, the sibling backend for larger shapes, threads `gemm1_clamp_limit`
  through its activation paths and was never affected.

**Relation to #53875.** That PR contains the same guard alongside a new fused CUDA kernel;
this PR is just the correctness guard, which was asked for separately in that thread so it
can land and be backported on its own. Close this one if #53875 lands first.

## Test Plan

`pytest tests/kernels/moe/test_block_fp8.py` on an H200, which now includes a dispatch
regression asserting the fused kernel is skipped when a clamp limit is set.

## Test Result

The new test fails before the fix and passes after. The rest of the suite is unchanged:
163 passed, and its 3 `test_w8a8_block_fp8_fused_moe` failures at N=4608/K=7168 reproduce
identically on unmodified `main`.

No model eval was run: the change routes clamped SiLU back onto the pre-#42497 unfused
path that the existing block-fp8 suites already cover. Separately, in our own deployment
(out-of-tree, `swiglu_limit = 10.0`, fp8 block quantization) this bug produced deterministic
junk-token argmaxes during decode, which the fix removes.

nodes.title: [Scheduler] Soften Long Prefill Tokens Threshhold
nodes.body:
## Purpose

`long_prefill_token_threshold` caps how many tokens a single prefill can take per step so that a long prompt doesn't starve other requests of the token budget. Today the cap is applied unconditionally, so a request that is alone in the scheduler is still chunked at the threshold even though there is nothing to starve — this just wastes the rest of `max_num_batched_tokens` and slows down TTFT for no benefit.

This PR skips the threshold when the request is the only one in the scheduler (`running` + `waiting` + `skipped_waiting` <= 1). As soon as any other request is present, the threshold applies as before.

Changes:
- `vllm/v1/core/sched/scheduler.py`: compute an effective `long_prefill_token_threshold` once per `schedule()` call (0 when there is a single request) and use it in both the running and waiting paths.
- `vllm/config/scheduler.py`: document the new behavior on `long_prefill_token_threshold`.
- `tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py`: add tests for the lone-request (uncapped) and multi-request (capped) cases.
- `tests/v1/core/test_deferred_block_free.py`: `test_abort_mid_prefill_defers_free` relied on the threshold to chunk a single request; switch it to `max_num_batched_tokens=16` so it still exercises a mid-prefill abort.

Not a duplicate: no open PR changes when `long_prefill_token_threshold` applies. Related PRs (#57427, #49075) add concurrent partial-prefill limits, which is a separate mechanism.

## Test Plan

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/v1/core/test_scheduler.py tests/v1/core/test_deferred_block_free.py -q
```

nodes.title: [Perf][Attention] Reduce GLM sparse MLA preparation overhead
nodes.body:
## Purpose

Reduce query packing and sparse-index preparation overhead around FlashInfer NoPE MLA attention.

The three commits:

1. Reuse a contiguous NoPE query when its rotary tail is empty, avoiding a redundant `torch.cat` before FP8 quantization. Preserve concatenation for nonempty rotary dimensions and strided queries.
2. Use one padded remap program per query for counted sparse capacities up to 4096. Initialize padding and reduce valid counts inside the remap kernel, removing separate fills and atomic accumulation. Preserve larger tiled cases and reusable buffers. Name the device entry point `sparse_mla_index_remap_kernel` for trace attribution.
3. Simplify empty-query handling: fuse dummy-entry preparation and safe-length calculation while preserving raw counts; skip preparation and masking for resident TP; mask only LSE for DCP and let its existing merge suppress zero-weight outputs, including NaNs. Preserve PyTorch output masking for HiSparse without LSE. There is no custom output-zeroing kernel.

Duplicate-work checks found no matching open PR. Related PRs #54258 (separate ROCm remap kernel), #38354 (DeepSeek pre-attention GEMM/RoPE fusion), and #57161 (GLM kpool/indexer scheduling) address different kernels or stages. No existing issue is being claimed or closed.

## Correctness

Prior TP validation on the experiment stack used GLM-5.3-Flash, TP8+EP8, all custom ops enabled, eager execution, no prefix cache, and exactly 32768 input tokens with either 1 or 16 generated tokens. Across 12 repeatability requests, all 8976 sparse-layer calls across eight ranks had positive valid counts (minimum 1). A direct full-shape FP8 attention comparison at 32768 queries × 8 heads × 512 dimensions, capacity 2176, matched the previous implementation bit for bit.

## Performance

Controlled end-to-end comparison on four GB300 GPUs, TP4+EP4, eager, `custom_ops=["all"]`, no prefix cache, no speculative decoding, and FP8 E4M3 KV cache. The actual upstream PR model stayed loaded while an idle-worker extension switched only the three preparation changes to their PR-base implementations. All four ranks verified the implementation selection. Compatible prebuilt extensions were reused.

Both implementations were warmed, then measured in four alternating baseline/PR and PR/baseline rounds with five matched samples per workload per round (20 pairs each). Each request had exactly 32768 input tokens, with a 32768-token prefill scheduling limit. Prefill generated one token; decode generated 128 tokens. These are client-observed serving latencies.

| Metric | PR base | PR | Latency reduction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 32K prefill TTFT, median | 518.25 ms | 507.61 ms | 2.05% |
| Decode inter-token latency, median | 122.85 ms/token | 120.77 ms/token | 1.70% |

All 20 pairs improved for each workload. Per-round median reductions ranged from 1.78–2.27% for prefill and 1.21–1.98% for decode. These measurements apply to eager TP4 execution; CUDA-graph decode and other parallel configurations were not measured in this comparison.

Earlier isolated measurements on the same GB300 GPU, using CUDA graph replay and the median of five samples with 40 repetitions/sample:

| Operation | Before | Optimized |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Remap including initialization | 531.90 µs | 282.93 µs |
| Safe lengths and dummy entry | 12.32 µs | 4.12 µs |

Shape: 32768 queries × 8 heads × 512 dimensions, capacity 2176. These are preparation microbenchmarks from the experiment stack. Resident TP now skips safe-length preparation entirely. Earlier tracing also confirmed removal of all 11 redundant query concatenations. The final upstream revision has not been reprofiled; the controlled end-to-end results above are separate from these older microbenchmarks. Measurements of the removed output-zeroing kernel are excluded.

nodes.title: [Bugfix] Annotate MTP draft KV cache groups positionally on the hybrid grouping path
nodes.body:
## Purpose

Hybrid attention + Mamba models using MTP, such as Qwen3.5 and Qwen3-Next, can reach the general KV-cache grouping path without identifying the drafter's group. Since #52771, `OffloadingConnector` deliberately treats unannotated groups as non-draft. The missing annotation therefore leaves the actual drafter-containing group without volatile trailing-chunk handling and produces a warning at startup.

Enable the existing trailing-layer annotation rule for `method="mtp"` on both the packed and general grouping paths, guarded by an exact partition of registered layers. For these hybrid layouts, identify the drafter-containing attention group, including when it also contains target layers, so the offloader excludes its volatile trailing chunk while Mamba groups remain unannotated. Preserve the existing `deepseek_v4` and `deepseek_v41` model checks so their `method="dspark"` path continues to identify the draft group. Other EAGLE/DSpark models retain their existing annotation behavior.

This extends the positional rule from #52047 and complements #52771 by supplying the missing group annotation. The separate #56026 proposes identifying all groups under a distinct drafter prefix. This PR retains the positional rule's limitation: when trailing drafter caches span several groups, it identifies only the group containing the last registered layer.

nodes.title: [Bugfix][GDN] Fix stateless first-chunk classification
nodes.body:
## Purpose

Fixes #51562.

`GDNMetadataBuilder.build()` passed `decode_threshold=1` to
`split_decodes_and_prefills()` while leaving
`treat_short_extends_as_decodes=True`. As a result, every one-token sequence was
classified as a decode, including the first chunk of a request with no prior GDN
state. The decode path then reads recurrent and convolution state unconditionally;
because Mamba-style state pages can be reused without being zeroed, that first token
could consume stale state from a previous request.

This change:

- classifies non-speculative one-token chunks from state availability
  (`seq_len <= query_len`) and the runner's `is_prefilling` signal;
- keeps resumed one-token chunks and CUDA graph capture dummy batches on the decode
  path;
- stages FULL CUDA graph metadata based on graph-compatible shape rather than the
  derived prefill/decode split, so mixed and all-stateless batches use persistent
  buffers correctly; and
- adds regression coverage for stateless first chunks, resumed one-token chunks,
  capture dummy metadata, and CUDA graph staging.

The fix lives in the shared GDN metadata builder and therefore covers its Qwen,
OLMo, InternS2, Bailing, and standalone Kimi-Linear users. Runner-level FULL CUDA
graph selection is a separate concern tracked by #47123; this PR does not duplicate
that broader runner change.

Duplicate-work check (2026-08-09): issue #51562 has no comments, and searches for
open PRs referencing `51562` or matching `GatedDeltaNet metadata stateless decode`
returned no results. Related PR #51483 changes the Kimi K3 subclass rather than this
shared builder.

AI assistance was used to inspect the issue, identify the root cause.  I reviewed the final diff and the test results below.The submitting author reviewed every changed line in the final diff.

## Test Plan

1. Run the GDN metadata builder unit tests.
2. Run Ruff lint and formatting checks on both changed files.
3. Before marking the PR ready, run an end-to-end affected-model evaluation with a
   freshly allocated/reused GDN state page and a one-token first chunk.

## Test Result

- Before the fix, the new stateless-first-chunk regression observed 3 decodes and 0
  prefills instead of 2 decodes and 1 prefill.
- `tests/v1/attention/test_gdn_metadata_builder.py`: **16 passed**, 14 existing
  PyTorch JIT deprecation warnings.

nodes.title: [CI] Add pre-commit check that new tests are tethered to Buildkite jobs
nodes.body:
## Purpose

Adds `check-test-tethering`, a pre-commit hook that fails when a file under
`tests/` is collected by **no** Buildkite job in any pipeline — i.e. it exists,
passes review, merges, and then never actually runs.

Prompted by @khluu's CI-coverage audit (and @njhill hitting the same thing a few
weeks back). @khluu's specific ask: a CI check that, when a test is added or
changed under `tests/`, verifies it's included in some Buildkite job; @njhill
added "and maybe something nightly which looks for any that have become
untethered somehow." This is that check.

## What it does

- **`tools/pre_commit/check_test_tethering.py`** parses every job (and each
  `mirror.amd` sub-step) in every Buildkite pipeline yaml — the pipeline
  directories are read from `.buildkite/ci_config*.yaml` (`job_dirs:`), currently
  `test_areas/`, `hardware_tests/` and `intel_jobs/` across the CUDA, ROCm and
  Intel pipelines, plus the legacy `.buildkite/test-amd.yaml` — and works out
  which test paths each `commands:` entry actually collects:
  - `pytest` positional args vs. `--ignore` (path prefix) / `--ignore-glob`
    (whole-path fnmatch, pytest semantics) / `--deselect`, with value-taking
    options (`-k`, `-m`, `--shard-id`, …) skipped, `::nodeid` selectors stripped,
    and glob path args honored;
  - `find <dir> -name 'test_*.py' [-not -name …] [-maxdepth N]` piped to
    `xargs pytest` or a terminated `-exec pytest … \;` (a `find` that doesn't
    actually reach pytest is not counted);
  - direct runners — `python`, `python3`, `torchrun`, `coverage <script>.py`
    (only the executed script, not its argv);
  - `bash <script>.sh` wrappers parsed one level deep, seeing through
    `env FOO=1 bash …` / `if ! … bash "$SCRIPT"` wrappers, `\`-continued lines,
    literal `VAR=path` expansion, and `${GIT_ROOT}/tests/…`-style absolute paths;
  - leading `FOO=bar` env-var assignments before the command are stripped
    (`test-amd.yaml` steps are full of `VLLM_TEST_FORCE_LOAD_FORMAT=auto pytest …`
    and `TP_SIZE=1 DP_SIZE=2 pytest …`).

  It's deliberately conservative — an unrecognised command contributes nothing
  rather than guessing, and a `-k`/`-m` filter does **not** count a file as
  un-run.

- **`tools/pre_commit/test_tethering_allowlist.txt`** — the ~49 test files that
  are untethered across every parsed pipeline on `main` today, grouped with
  reasons. Append-only under protest; the intent is that it only ever shrinks. A
  full-tree run also reports allowlist entries that have since become tethered,
  or whose file is gone, so the list can't rot.

### Modes

| trigger | behaviour |
|---|---|
| changed test files (normal pre-commit) | each must be tethered or allowlisted |
| `--all`, or the change set touches a pipeline yaml / a `ci_config` / the allowlist | full-tree scan (a job-command edit can orphan a test not in the diff) |

vLLM's pre-commit CI runs `pre-commit run --all-files`, so **every gated PR
already gets the full scan** — that covers @njhill's "nightly sweep" without a
separate Buildkite job. The full scan is well under a second for ~1500 test
files across ~60 pipeline yamls (pure Python + PyYAML, one `git ls-files`, no
network).

New untethered files are always fatal. Stale/dangling allowlist entries are
advisory in a PR run (so an unrelated PR isn't blocked by cleanup) and fatal
only under an explicit `--all`.

The hook runs inside the existing `pre-commit` workflow, which is already gated
on a `ready`/`ready-run-all-tests`/`verified` label or an established author, so
it adds no attack surface for drive-by PRs.

### Which pipelines count

The question the hook asks is "does *some* Buildkite job run this test", not
"which pipeline". The pipeline directories aren't hard-coded — they're read from
`.buildkite/ci_config*.yaml`'s `job_dirs:`, the same lists Buildkite itself uses
to assemble each pipeline, so `hardware_tests/` and `intel_jobs/` count
alongside `test_areas/` (and a new job dir is picked up automatically). The
legacy `.buildkite/test-amd.yaml` is appended while the AMD migration into
`test_areas/` finishes — guarded on the file existing (`TEST_AMD_YAML.is_file()`),
so it drops out with no code change once removed, flagging whatever the migration
left behind.

## Not a duplicate

`gh pr list --search "test tethering" / "untethered tests"` — nothing open.
@DarkLight1337 said he'd open a PR to wire up `tests/entrypoints/cohere/`, and
@mgoin is looking at the `tests/models/` ones — those are the *fixes* for
specific gaps; this PR is the *gate* that stops new ones. Complementary.

## Testing

**Cross-checked against @khluu's four manual audit threads (2026-09-01):**

| thread | tool agreement |
|---|---|
| overall audit | matches |
| `tests/entrypoints/` | all cohere/* + `test_offline_utils.py` flagged; `test_chat_utils` (real path `entrypoints/unit_tests/`) correctly reported tethered — answers @DarkLight1337's question in-thread. After his fix merged, the tool now reports cohere/* should come off the allowlist. |
| `tests/models/` (7 files) | exact match, no misses, no extras |
| `tests/distributed/` | every file @khluu listed flagged, incl. `test_flashinfer_pcie_ipc_all_reduce.py` |

**The allowlist self-heals — demonstrated live.** Rebasing this branch across
~140 commits of `main`: the tool reported all 7 `cohere/*` entries as now
tethered (remove them), `test_offline_utils.py` as deleted (remove it), and
flagged 3 genuinely new gaps that had merged in the meantime —
`test_flashinfer_pcie_ipc_all_reduce.py` (#53576), `test_weight_transfer_nccl_uid.py`
(#53784, a sibling of the already-tethered `test_weight_transfer.py` that wasn't
added to the same job), and `tests/platforms/test_cpu.py` (#52191, a new dir).
All three are exactly the failure mode this hook prevents.

**Run against the 12 most recently merged PRs** (post `test-amd.yaml` support):
every `tests/` file they touched is tethered; one earlier sweep of ~80 commits
surfaced `tests/rocm/test_moe_weight_replay.py` (#46009), wired only into
`test-amd.yaml`'s `(MI300) Quantization` group at a reviewer's request — now
correctly recognised as tethered rather than flagged.

**Parser battery (`tests/tools/test_check_test_tethering.py`, 125 cases,
hand-crafted + real-tree):**
- pytest shapes: dir sweep / nested / exact file / sibling-not-matched;
  `--ignore=` dir, `--ignore` (space) file, `--ignore-glob` crossing `/`
  (pytest semantics), ignore-doesn't-over-exclude; multiple positional paths
  incl. bare root files; `-k`/`-m` don't un-tether; `-m` value not mistaken for
  a path; env-var prefix + `$$SHARD` flags; glob path args (match + non-match);
  `::nodeid` stripped; `./` and `tests/` prefixes.
- `find` → pytest: name globs, `-maxdepth 1`, `-not -name`; a terminated
  `-exec pytest … \;` counts, an unterminated one or `xargs echo pytest` does
  not; `xargs env FOO=1 pytest` resolves through the wrapper; a `find` piped to
  `wc`, or a `pytest` in a separate `;`/`&&` command, does not arm the sweep.
- direct runners: `python3 <file>`, `torchrun <file>`, `coverage`; only the
  executed script counts (`--suffix v1` argv must not tether `tests/v1/`);
  `--nproc-per-node` / `timeout -k` values not treated as paths.
- `bash <script>.sh`: followed through `env FOO=1 bash` / `if ! … bash "$SCRIPT"`
  wrappers, `\`-continued lines, literal `VAR=path` expansion (but not inside
  `'single quotes'`), `${GIT_ROOT}/tests/…` prefixes; `bash -c '<code>' x.sh`
  does *not* follow `x.sh` ($0, not run); `echo x.sh` / `cp a.sh b` don't.
- shell noise (`export …`, `pip install …`, missing `.sh`) contributes nothing.
- synthetic yaml: NVIDIA step, `--ignore` honored, `mirror.amd`-only command
  picked up, singular `command:` key, `test-amd.yaml` coverage tethers, missing
  `test-amd.yaml` is not fatal, non-mapping yaml is a loud error, `job_dirs`
  read from a synthetic `ci_config.yaml` (a broken config falls back).
- real-tree invariants: >1000 modules, >200 selections, every allowlist entry
  currently untethered and present on disk, idempotent, malformed command
  doesn't crash, no selection matches everything.
- CLI exit codes: `--all` → 0 (allowlist current); tethered / allowlisted /
  non-existent path → 0; new orphan → 1.

**Framework:**
```
pre-commit run check-test-tethering --all-files    # Passed (CI's exact invocation)
pre-commit run mypy-3.10  --files …                # Passed
```
plus a live negative test: deleting the only `pytest test_regression.py` command
from `misc.yaml` and running the hook on just that yaml → fails, names
`tests/test_regression.py`.

No model-affecting changes.

## AI assistance

Written with Claude (Claude Code). All logic, the allowlist, and every test
above were reviewed line-by-line by me.

nodes.title: [Kimi-K3][AMD] Return KDA and MLA projection outputs directly
nodes.body:
## Purpose

Kimi-K3's AMD attention paths copied each output projection into a caller-owned buffer even though the projection already returns a tensor with the required shape, dtype, layout, and lifetime.

This PR removes that redundant post-projection allocation and copy from both attention families:

- 69 KDA layers
- 24 MLA layers
- 93 post-attention-projection copies per model step in total

The functionality from #50847 is now folded into this PR. #50654 is separate and complementary: it optimizes the earlier KDA recurrent/conv/RMSNorm path, while this PR removes the later copy after the output projection.

## Implementation

- Return KDA output-projection storage directly from both the shared KDA implementation and the dedicated full-rank Kimi-K3 implementation selected by current `main`.
- Return MLA output-projection storage directly.
- Use one return-value contract in `KimiDecoderLayer` for KDA and MLA.
- Preserve attention arithmetic, state updates, normalization, projection, tensor-parallel communication, and HIP-graph replay behavior.

## Validation

```text
Targeted ownership tests:  3 passed
Ruff 0.14.0 check:         passed
Ruff 0.14.0 format check:  passed
git diff --check:          passed
DCO:                       passed
```

The tests cover KDA dispatch ownership, the concrete full-rank Kimi-K3 KDA forward path, and MLA dispatch ownership. In each case, the returned tensor is the exact projection tensor and has the same `data_ptr()`.

## Fixed-cohort decode A/B

### Setup

```text
GPU:                 8 x AMD Instinct MI355X (gfx950)
Parallelism:         TP8
Model:               Kimi-K3, BF16 activations / MXFP4 weights

Success rate:        240/240 measured requests
```

Both variants used image `localhost/kimi-pp8-upstream-clean` (vLLM `beca88e59`, AITER `99733dc00`). The baseline was the unmodified image. The candidate mounted only this PR's AMD runtime files from `43d81ba3e`. The relevant AMD Kimi-K3 files in the image are identical to the rebased `main` baseline before this PR.

### Results

Means over three measured runs. TPOT and ITL are end-to-end serving metrics, not the reviewer's pure-GPU trace period.

| Cohort | Metric | Baseline | Combined PR | Delta |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| C16 | Mean TPOT | 73.141 ms | 72.428 ms | **-0.713 ms (-0.97%)** |
| C16 | Median ITL | 70.488 ms | 70.186 ms | **-0.302 ms** |
| C16 | Output throughput | 193.575 tok/s | 195.555 tok/s | **+1.02%** |
| C24 | Mean TPOT | 74.958 ms | 74.457 ms | **-0.501 ms (-0.67%)** |
| C24 | Median ITL | 71.311 ms | 70.916 ms | **-0.396 ms** |

nodes.title: [Bugfix][Spec Decode] Cap DFlash/DSpark profiling query batch
nodes.body:
Fixes #56443.

## Root Cause
The memory-profiling dummy run can hand-build max_num_seqs requests without applying the scheduler's speculative query-token budget. For DSpark/DFlash, each request can require num_query_per_req draft query rows.
For example, with max_num_seqs=512, max_num_batched_tokens=2048, and DSpark K=5, the profiling path asks the speculator for 512 * 5 = 2560 query rows while its input buffers are sized for 2048 rows, so DSpark can read _anchor_idx past input_ids and later surface CUDA IndexKernel/device-side assert errors.

## Changes
Cap the initial dummy/profile draft-generation pass to the largest complete set of query blocks that fits the speculator input buffer, preserve the full target-context and sampler projection for memory profiling, and fail early with a clear ValueError if a real query batch exceeds the input buffer.

Other profiling dummy runs, including FlashInfer autotune, build target attention metadata and cannot use the initial skip-attention shortcut. Add a default no-op speculator hook that lets DFlash-family speculators cap the dummy request count before GPUModelRunner builds those synthetic batches. This does not affect real serving requests or other speculator implementations.

## Existing PRs

#53970 addresses the same `max_num_seqs * parallel-draft query width > max_num_batched_tokens` failure condition with a broader capacity-based fix: it raises `max_num_batched_tokens` to cover the worst-case parallel-draft batch and enlarges the DFlash input buffers. This PR instead leaves the configured target token budget unchanged and caps only synthetic profiling batches to the existing speculator capacity. It covers both the initial skip-attention memory profile and full-attention profiling dummy runs such as FlashInfer autotune, and adds a fail-fast check if a real serving batch violates the scheduler invariant already established by #51256. The approaches are alternatives for the startup crash, but differ in scope and memory/scheduling impact.

#53080 separates target and draft scheduler budgets, but it does not constrain model-runner-generated profiling batches that bypass normal scheduler admission. #53577 covers broader DSpark/PP and padded graph safety work, but it has no matching profile query-buffer cap. #55133 and #56387 address different DSpark failure modes.

nodes.title: [ROCm][Bugfix] Explicitly reject FSE=1 with DPA+ETP deployment for DeepSeek-V4

## Purpose

Running DeepSeek-V4 on ROCm with data-parallel attention (`--data-parallel-size 8`) and `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1` fails during weight loading with an obscure error.

```bash
File "/.../vllm/vllm/models/deepseek_v4/amd/model.py", line 1243, in load_weights
    param = params_dict[name_mapped]
KeyError: 'layers.0.ffn.experts.routed_experts.w13_weight_scale_inv'
```

Fused shared experts are not supported under data parallelism: the fused path has no way to load the FP8 shared expert into the MXFP4 routed slot, so users end up debugging weight loading instead of the configuration.

This PR fails fast at model construction time: when fused shared experts are requested (`VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1`), expert parallelism is off, and `data_parallel_size > 1`, the model now raises:

```bash
ValueError: DeepSeek-V4 fused shared experts (VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1) are not supported with data parallelism (data_parallel_size > 1). Set VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=0 to run the shared expert as an unfused FP8 MLP.
```

The check lives in `_fuse_shared_experts_enabled()` in the ROCm-only model file (`vllm/models/deepseek_v4/amd/model.py`), so non-ROCm paths are untouched. Configurations where FSE is already silently disabled (e.g. expert parallelism enabled) do not raise.

## Test Plan

Launch the DPA+ETP server with `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=1`.

## Test Result

Directly raise `ValueError` so that users know they need to set `VLLM_ROCM_USE_AITER_FUSION_SHARED_EXPERTS=0` for this scenario, instead of debugging the weight loading code.

nodes.title: [Spec Decode] Enable async scheduling for DFlash
nodes.body:
## Scope

Adds `dflash` to the async-scheduling allowlist in `VllmConfig`, on both the explicit `--async-scheduling` path (previously a hard `ValueError`) and the default auto-enable path (previously force-disabled with a warning). The V2 model runner's async machinery (async output copies, GPU-side draft-token buffers) is method-agnostic, and the DFlash speculator consumes the same GPU tensors (`num_sampled`, `num_rejected`, `last_sampled`) as the DSpark one, so no engine changes beyond the allowlist are needed.


## Configuration

No new configuration. With default settings, async scheduling now stays enabled for `--speculative-config '{"method":"dflash", ...}'` instead of being silently disabled. `--no-async-scheduling` still forces it off.

## Launch command

<details>
<summary>vllm serve command used for validation (GB200, TP4)</summary>

```bash
vllm serve Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 -tp 4 \
  --max-num-seqs 32 --max-num-batched-tokens 8192 \
  --language-model-only \
  --compilation-config '{"pass_config": {"fuse_allreduce_rms": false}}' \
  --speculative-config '{"method":"dflash","model":"z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2","num_speculative_tokens":7,"attention_backend":"TRITON_ATTN"}'
```

(The `fuse_allreduce_rms` workaround is unrelated to this PR: the DFlash2 candidate selector trips a piecewise-compile assert when the allreduce-RMS fusion splits compile ranges at TP4. The TRITON_ATTN draft backend is used because the FLASH_ATTN path is broken for this draft/target pair — FA4-hd256 page-size clash with the hybrid target's mamba-forced KV block size.)

</details>

## Validation

- New unit test `test_dflash_allows_async_scheduling` in `tests/test_config.py`: builds a minimal DFlash2 draft config and asserts async scheduling stays enabled (previously force-disabled). Run: `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_config.py -k "dflash or async_scheduling" -q` → 5 passed. `pre-commit run --files vllm/config/vllm.py tests/test_config.py` → all passed (ruff check + format included).
- E2E correctness on 4xGB200 TP4, Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B + z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2 draft (7 speculative tokens, standard rejection, greedy draft, async scheduling on): GSM8K 5-shot flexible-extract 0.9708 / strict-match 0.9704, matching the no-spec baseline 0.9719/0.9716 and the DSpark draft 0.9708/0.9712. Measured acceptance length 5.96 on GSM8K traffic. Repeated with prefix caching enabled (default): 0.9735 / 0.9735 — the hybrid-mamba + prefix-cache + spec-decode path is also correct.

## Performance

Same-build A/B, bs=1 pure-decode (ISL=1, OSL=1000, 2 warmup + 4 requests, `vllm bench serve`, 4xGB200 TP4, DFlash2 with TRITON_ATTN draft backend fully CUDA-graphed, synthetic acceptance length 6):

| async scheduling | TPOT (mean) | decode tok/s |
|---|---|---|
| off (`--no-async-scheduling`) | 2.127 ms | 470.2 |
| on (default with this PR) | 1.510 ms | 662.3 |

**+41% decode throughput (1.41x lower TPOT) at bs=1** with DFlash2 enabled.

## Notes

AI assistance was used for this change (code, tests, and validation); all quoted results were produced by actually running the commands above.

Duplicate-work check: `gh pr list --search "dflash async"` and `gh search prs "async scheduling" "dflash"` over vllm-project/vllm return no open or merged PR enabling async scheduling for DFlash; the allowlist in `vllm/config/vllm.py` on master still excludes it. The sibling DSpark was allowlisted in its original PR (#46995); nothing since covers DFlash.

nodes.title: [Rust Frontend] Introduce parser-owned output grammar interfaces
[Security] Reject min_tokens that exceeds the filled max_tokens default
nodes.body:
## Summary
`SamplingParams` skips the `min_tokens <= max_tokens` check while `max_tokens` is unset. The input processor then fills `max_tokens` from `max_model_len` and forwards the request, so an explicit null `max_tokens` with an oversized `min_tokens` is only validated when EngineCore reconstructs the params. That validation error is uncaught on the input-socket thread and wedges the engine. This change re-checks `min_tokens` immediately after filling the default and rejects the request.

## Changes
- `vllm/v1/engine/input_processor.py`: after filling unset `max_tokens`, reject `min_tokens` that exceeds the filled value.
- `tests/test_request_input_bounds.py`: unit coverage for the reject and for an in-range `min_tokens` after fill.
- `tests/entrypoints/scale_out/token_in_token_out/test_serving_tokens.py`: generate-endpoint regression for explicit null `max_tokens` plus a follow-up request that must still succeed.

## Codepath coverage
- `/inference/v1/generate`, OpenAI `/v1` generate routes, `/invocations`, offline `LLMEngine` / `AsyncLLM`, and streaming-input adds all go through `InputProcessor.process_inputs`.
- Rust HTTP/gRPC already rejects `min_tokens` above the resolved `max_tokens` in `lower_sampling_params`.

## Duplicate-work check
Searched open and merged PRs for `min_tokens`, `process_input_sockets`, `input_processor max_tokens`, and generate sampling validation.
- https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/54175 bounds a client-supplied `max_tokens` against int32 overflow on the generate route; it does not re-check `min_tokens` after a null `max_tokens` is filled.
- https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/53357 maps `verify()` `ValueError`s to client errors; it does not add this bound.
- https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55164 validates sampling-param list size limits.
- https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/46733 (merged) is the Rust frontend `min_tokens` check only.

No open or merged PR closes this Python fill-then-forward path.

## Tests
- `test_unset_max_tokens_rejects_oversized_min_tokens` — construction with unset `max_tokens` and oversized `min_tokens` is rejected after fill.
- `test_unset_max_tokens_accepts_min_tokens_within_filled_max` — in-range `min_tokens` still proceeds with the filled default.
- `test_generate_rejects_min_tokens_above_filled_max_tokens` — generate route returns 400 and a later request succeeds.

nodes.title: [Bugfix][Frontend] Validate mixed prompt embedding mask lengths
nodes.body:
## Purpose

Reject a `prompt_is_token_ids` mask whose length differs from the number of prompt embedding rows before submitting the request to the engine.

For example, a Python mixed-embedding prompt with three embedding rows, three token IDs, and a two-element mask currently passes input processing and reaches a NumPy broadcast error in `InputBatch.add_request()`. A one-element mask can instead broadcast silently. The mask describes each prompt position, so both inputs should be rejected at admission.

This adds the check to `InputProcessor` and reports `VLLMValidationError` with `parameter="prompt_is_token_ids"`. Requests without a mask and correctly aligned mixed prompts retain their existing behavior.

I checked related work and did not find an existing fix for this admission check. #54509 fixes mask alignment during truncation; #56656 adds the mask to prefix-cache keys. #51891 touches input validation, but its mask-length condition controls embedding replacement positions and does not reject a mismatched mask.

## Test Plan

The regression tests exercise `InputProcessor.process_inputs()` with empty, short, broadcastable, and long masks. They also cover pure embeddings, token IDs plus embeddings without a mask, and an aligned mixed prompt.

```bash
VLLM_TARGET_DEVICE=cpu PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1 \
  HF_HUB_OFFLINE=1 TRANSFORMERS_OFFLINE=1 \
  .venv/bin/python -m pytest \
  tests/test_request_input_bounds.py \
  tests/renderers/test_chat_utils_prompt_embeds.py \
  tests/v1/engine/test_input_processor_trace_replay.py -q -p no:cacheprovider

.venv/bin/pre-commit run --files \
  vllm/v1/engine/input_processor.py tests/test_request_input_bounds.py
.venv/bin/pre-commit run mypy-3.12 --hook-stage manual --files \
  vllm/v1/engine/input_processor.py tests/test_request_input_bounds.py
```

## Test Result

- Before the fix, the new cases produced **4 failed, 3 passed**: all four malformed masks were accepted.
- With the fix, the three suites above produced **123 passed**.
- All applicable pre-commit hooks and the manual mypy 3.12 check passed.
- A10 / Qwen3.5-0.8B (BF16, eager, prefix caching disabled): the baseline legacy runner reproduced the broadcast error; the next normal request returned `EngineDeadError` as well.
- With the fix, the legacy and V2 runners each passed **11 checks**: three valid generation controls, four rejected mask lengths (0, 1, 2, 4), and successful normal generation after each rejection. The valid controls produced the same token IDs before/after the fix and across runners.

nodes.title: [RL][Sleep] Retain frozen weights across level-2 sleep
nodes.body:
## Purpose

Level-2 sleep discards weights, including frozen parameters omitted by the
trainer. Preserve selected parameters so they remain usable after wake-up
without retransmission.

`sleep_preserve_parameter_names` (CLI: `--sleep-preserve-parameter-names`) matches runtime parameter names
with globs (default: empty; unmatched patterns raise). Selected GPU parameters
are backed up to pageable CPU memory and restored in place on weights wake-up;
CPU-resident parameters need no copy. Backups are released after restoration.
Level-1 behavior is unchanged. The option lives in `ModelConfig` alongside the
other sleep settings and does not require a weight-transfer engine.

Two private Worker methods keep selection and backup state within the sleep/wake lifecycle. XPU inherits the implementation; CPU workers do not support sleep. Selection
covers the target model only. The trainer must omit selected weights, and
reload/post-processing must preserve their values and storage. Budget host
memory for backups; this option does not filter updates.

## Validation

### Focused checks

- Empty selection, CPU-resident parameters, unmatched-pattern rejection,
  in-place restoration, and backup release passed.
- Commit hooks passed, including Ruff and mypy; `git diff --check` passed.

### Real GPU sleep/wake

On an NVIDIA GB200 using the real CuMem sleep backend and a small Llama model:

- Three level-2 cycles retained `lm_head.weight`. All 16,384 bytes and its GPU
  `data_ptr` remained exact after every wake, while a non-retained parameter was
  changed each cycle.
- Level-1 sleep preserved all 180,864 parameter bytes and addresses.
- With the default empty selection, no parameter was backed up and a complete
  reload restored all 180,864 bytes.

Commands run in the pinned serving container:

```bash
python3 /opt/test_frozen_gpu.py configured
python3 /opt/test_frozen_gpu.py empty
```

Both returned `PASS`. After moving the option to `ModelConfig`, the same GPU
tests were rerun with `weight_transfer_config=None`.

The integration results below precede the configuration relocation; the GPU
sleep/wake regression above exercises the current implementation.

### Default VERL update path

An eight-rank run exercised VERL's standard non-layerwise update path. The
trainer omitted four frozen weight/scale tensors per rank. Across all ranks,
32 CPU-resident tensors totaling 202,758,032,400 bytes retained their complete
SHA-256 digest, `data_ptr`, shape, dtype, and device through level-2 sleep and
two updates. All eight trainable shards changed after an optimizer step, and
the subsequent synchronization did not mutate trainer state.

Generation succeeded before and after the update. On the same 30-question
held-out math set, pre/post accuracy was 8/30; all eight non-truncated responses
were correct in both runs. This is integration evidence, not an isolated model
accuracy claim.

### Cross-host TP8

A two-host NVIDIA GB200 test ran TP8 with four ranks per host and default
`FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` CUDA Graphs. Across two real level-2 cycles, the same 32
CPU-resident tensors retained complete SHA-256 digests and addresses both before
and after restoring the other weights. All three generations produced identical
token IDs. There was no OOM and no CUDA Graph invalidation or recapture during
reload.

XPU execution remains untested.

## Duplicate checks

Reviewed #50079 and open sleep/retention PRs. This preserves selected parameters
across level-2 sleep; #55206 releases cached pinned memory and #49789 preserves
post-load runtime state.

AI assistance was used. Human review of the latest revision remains pending.

nodes.title: [Bugfix][Qwen2.5-VL] Honor video fps for temporal M-RoPE
nodes.body:
## Purpose

Qwen2.5-VL currently loses video metadata before calling the HuggingFace processor. Since the HF video processor refactor, `second_per_grid_ts` is computed from `video_metadata.sampled_fps`; when vLLM drops that metadata, pre-decoded videos fall back to a default sampled fps instead of the request/video fps. That value drives the temporal M-RoPE scale used by the model, so videos tagged at 1fps and 30fps get the same temporal spacing in vLLM.

This fixes the Qwen2.5-VL path by keeping video metadata in the data parser, splitting `(video, metadata)` tuples before the HF processor call, and forwarding `video_metadata` so HF can compute `sampled_fps` from the real frame metadata. The dummy video builder also attaches synthetic metadata, matching the Qwen3-VL pattern and keeping memory profiling inputs valid once metadata is required.

Scope: the Qwen2.5-VL processor path. Qwen2-VL does not capture `second_per_grid_ts` in the same way, so that would be a separate change. vLLM's video loader already attaches metadata for URL/file inputs; the changed behavior is that bare pre-decoded video arrays without metadata now fail clearly instead of silently using a fallback fps.

Duplicate-work check: I did not find an open PR covering Qwen2.5-VL video metadata forwarding. PR #23058 is Qwen2.5-Omni only, PR #43198 only lets video frame sampling use a request `fps` override, PR #45555 only adds loader-side metadata that this path still dropped, and PR #47407 only bounds M-RoPE positions.

## Test Plan

nodes.title: [Rust Frontend] Build full-output grammars from initialized reasoning parsers
nodes.body:
## Purpose

Strict tool grammars currently start after the engine detects the end of reasoning. This change builds the reasoning phase from the initialized Rust parser and composes it with the visible-output grammar, allowing XGrammar to constrain the generated stream from token zero.

Step 2, following the merged #55269. That PR introduces the parser-owned grammar interfaces and request lifecycle; this follow-up activates `FromTokenZero` coverage for supported delimited reasoning parsers. The open-PR search found no separate implementation of this layer.

- Build the reasoning continuation from the final prompt state, including model-specific closing separators and any separator suffix remaining after prompt prefill.
- Enable the wrapper for DeepSeek R1/V3, Qwen3, GLM45, Step3/Step3.5, Nemotron V3, and HY3/HY4 through their existing parser implementations and aliases.
- Project the MiniMax M2 builder to its visible-output grammar before composing the reasoning wrapper, with an explicit check of the expected builder prefix.
- Preserve the existing tool-grammar activation policy. Supported requests use `reasoning_ended = Some(true)` through Step 1's lowering; the grammar requires the reasoning close before entering visible output.

K3, Gemma4, Inkling, and Harmony remain follow-up work.

## Test Plan

The builder-parity invariant is:

```text
reasoning-wrapped visible tool tag = builder output with the matching reasoning mode
```

`assert_builder_parity` checks 54 cases: nine reasoning/tool parser pairs × `ReasoningMode::{Enabled, Auto}` × required/named/strict-auto tool choices. Enabled initializes inside a prefilled reasoning block; Auto initializes without a reasoning boundary. Every case asserts `FromTokenZero` coverage. The comparison flattens nested sequences and ignores `AnyText.excludes`, including inside `Optional`, while retaining token and character budgets. It checks normalized grammar structure.

## Test Result

- After restacking onto main with #55269 merged: **1513 parser/chat/text/server/LLM/engine-client tests passed, 1 skipped**, including production renderer/parser roundtrips; XGrammar structural tags 0.3.0.
- Auto parity was confirmed failing before extending normalization into `Optional`, then all **54 cases passed** with the recursive normalization.
- Strict Clippy, formatting, and diff checks passed.
- Earlier local XGrammar 0.2.7 validation: 18 HY3/HY4 grammar configurations passed 72 token-mask/acceptance/stop replays with a controlled vocabulary; 9 HY3 configurations passed 36 replays with its cached model tokenizer.
### Prior GPU end-to-end regression checks

Paired GB200 runs on September 17–18 compared Step 1 [`ef67e07c`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/ef67e07c686c0e758815701d239a28e48da1e169) with Step 2 [`b38299c9`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/b38299c9fa958ac1471a77455969868457153d4b), using the same checkpoint, requests, and serving settings within each pair. The following model/parser configurations had **zero candidate-only task failures in the evaluated samples**. Success requires the expected answer and tool/direct-text behavior, with completion within the output budget. Counts show Step 1 → Step 2; existing failures remain included.

| Model family / tested checkpoint | Reasoning parser | Tool / unified parser | Paired GPU e2e result |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3: Qwen3-4B | `qwen3` | `qwen3_xml` | Native tasks 33/33 → 33/33; GSM8K 14/16 → 15/16; explicit starting states 21/21 → 21/21 |
| Qwen3.5: Qwen3.5-4B | `qwen3` | `qwen3_coder` | Native tasks 33/33 → 33/33; GSM8K 15/16 → 16/16; explicit starting states 21/21 → 21/21 |
| Qwen3.5: Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-FP8 | `qwen3` | `qwen3_coder` | Native tasks 33/33 → 33/33; GSM8K 15/16 → 16/16; explicit starting states 21/21 → 21/21 |
| GLM4.7: GLM-4.7-Flash | `glm47` | `glm47` | Native tasks 27/33 → 29/33; GSM8K 13/16 → 13/16; explicit starting states 11/12 → 11/12 |
| DeepSeek V4: DeepSeek-V4-Flash | `deepseek_v4` | `deepseek_v4` | Native tasks 33/33 → 33/33; GSM8K 15/16 → 15/16; explicit starting states 11/12 → 11/12 |
| DeepSeek V3.2: DeepSeek-V3.2 | `deepseek_v3` | `deepseek_v32` | Combined semantic suite 112/117 → 112/117; identical five failed cases |
| DeepSeek V4.1: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash | `deepseek_v41` | `deepseek_v41` | Combined semantic suite 114/117 → 115/117 |

Coverage includes required/named/strict-auto tool choice, reasoning modes and prompt-derived starting states, streaming, quoted reasoning delimiters, direct answers, sampled generation, a 16-question GSM8K sample, and real three-turn tool conversations. All listed checkpoints completed the three-turn flow 3/3 in both arms. The combined semantic suites exclude a separate deliberately insufficient 16-token truncation probe.
